# The Reality War
## Executive Summary
"The Reality War" stands as a pivotal cultural and narrative artifact within the twenty-first-century canon of British science fiction. Primarily, the title refers to the eighth and final episode of the fifteenth series of *Doctor Who* (marketed as Season 2 on Disney+), broadcast on May 31, 2025\. Written by showrunner Russell T Davies and directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai, the broadcast garnered significant attention for concluding the tenure of Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor, radically altering established lore regarding the Time Lord race, and reintroducing seminal figures such as Omega and The Rani. The episode's conclusion, featuring a regeneration into a character portrayed by Billie Piper, ignited widespread discourse regarding the future trajectory of the franchise .

Secondarily, the title designs a two-part science fiction novel series authored by Tim C. Taylor and published in 2012\. While unrelated narratively to the television show, Taylor's *The Reality War* shares thematic DNA in its exploration of rival realities vying for dominance, a synchronicity that highlights the enduring appeal of ontological conflict in speculative fiction .

This report provides an exhaustive analysis of both entities, prioritizing the television production's narrative mechanics, production context, critical reception, and lore implications, while also documenting the literary work to distinguish the two properties.

## ---

**Part I: Doctor Who – "The Reality War" (TV Story)**

### 1\. Production Context and Development
#### 1.1 The "Whoniverse" and the Disney+ Era
"The Reality War" represents the turning point of a specific phase in the history of *Doctor Who* , often referred to as the "Whoniverse" era. Following the partnership between the BBC and Disney Branded Television, the program undergoes a significant rebranding and budget injection. This finale, airing in May 2025, served as a litmus test for the new co-production model. Industry analysis noted that the high-concept nature of the episode—featuring expansive CGI environments like the "Bone Palace" and the "Underverse"—was indicative of the increased resources available to showrunner Russell T Davies .

The episode was positioned as the finale of "Season 2" (Series 15), following the 2024 Christmas special "Joy to the World" and the preceding seven episodes of the season. The narrative architecture was designed to bridge the gap between the classic series' mythology and the modern "Timeless Child" era, attempting to synthesize disparate strands of continuity into a cohesive, albeit controversial, whole .

#### 1.2 Writing and Directorial Vision
Russell T Davies, returning as showrunner, penned the script with a focus on high-stakes melodrama and "meta-narrative" commentary. Critics observed that the script was "relentlessly bonkers," a hallmark of Davies' strategy to compete in a crowded streaming landscape by generating "watercooler moments" . The direction by Alex Sanjiv Pillai was tasked with balancing intimate character drama—specifically the exit of companions Belinda Chandra and Ruby Sunday—with the maximalist spectacle of inter-dimensional warfare .

The production team, including Executive Producers Jane Tranter, Joel Collins, Phil Collinson, and Julie Gardner, orchestrated a complex shoot that required secrecy regarding the returning cast. The filming of the regeneration sequence and the cameos by Jodie Whittaker and Billie Piper were conducted under strict "closed set" protocols to prevent leaks, a strategy that largely succeeded in preserving the shock value of the broadcast .

#### 1.3 Musical Score
Composer Murray Gold provided the score for the episode, creating a soundscape that merged new motifs with nostalgic themes. The track "The Reality War" was released as part of the official soundtrack, noted for its bombastic choral arrangements suited to the return of Omega . Fans and audiophiles identified the reuse of themes from "The Doctor Falls" during the emotional climax, specifically during the Fifteenth Doctor's sacrifice, which served to underscore the cyclical nature of the Doctor's life and death .

### 2\. Narrative Architecture and Plot Analysis
#### 2.1 The Setup: "Wish World" and the Cliffhanger
To understand the events of "The Reality War," one must contextualize them within the two-part finale structure. The preceding episode, "Wish World," established a divergent reality created by the "Unholy Trinity": the two incarnations of The Rani and their human associate Conrad Clark. They utilized a "Magic Baby"—a psychic construct capable of altering reality based on wishes—to rewrite history. This resulted in a dystopia where the Doctor was erased or marginalized, setting the stage for a restoration narrative .

#### 2.2 Act I: The Time Hotel and the Rescue
The episode commences immediately following the cliffhanger of "Wish World," with the Fifteenth Doctor plummeting from a great height, seemingly to his death. The resolution to this peril introduces a key location: The Time Hotel. Anita Benn (Steph de Whalley), previously introduced as a hotel manager in the Christmas special "Joy to the World," reappears as the manager of this inter-dimensional sanctuary .

The Time Hotel functions as a "reality bunker," existing in a "real-time" future space that is impervious to the waves of reality distortion affecting the rest of the universe. This plot device allows the Doctor to survive the fall and retain his memories of the true timeline. Anita's intervention is not merely a deus ex machina but a callback to the Doctor's previous acts of kindness, reinforcing the theme that the Doctor's benevolent history is his greatest resource .

From the safety of the Time Hotel, the Doctor and Anita launch a counter-offensive. They open dimensional doors directly into the headquarters of UNIT (Unified Intelligence Taskforce). This action creates a "cross-draught" of reality—a metaphysical airflow that flushes the "Wish World" delusion out of the UNIT base. Key personnel, including Kate Lethbridge-Stewart, Colonel Ibrahim, and Shirley Anne Bingham, are instantaneously restored to their factory settings, regaining their memories and agency .

#### 2.3 Act II: The Unholy Trinity and the Omni-Sterility Retcon
With his allies restored, the Doctor confronts the antagonists. The "Unholy Trinity" pays a visit to UNIT Tower, leading to a crucial expository sequence. The villains are revealed to be:

1. **Mrs. Flood (Anita Dobson):** Revealed as an incarnation of The Rani, a renegade Time Lord scientist. 
2. **The Bi-generated Rani (Archie Panjabi):** A younger, concurrent incarnation created through the same bi-generation process that produced the Fifteenth Doctor. 
3. **Conrad Clark (Jonah Hauer-King):** A human antagonist with a personal connection to Ruby Sunday .

The Ranis reveal their motivation: **The Sterility of the Time Lords.** In a massive retcon of previous continuity, they assert that all Gallifreyans have become sterile and that natural reproduction is impossible. This revelation drives their plot to resurrect Omega, the stellar engineer and founder of Time Lord society, believing his mastery of antimatter and genetic engineering is the only path to rebuilding their race .

The Doctor challenges this assertion by pointing to **Poppy**, the child of his companion Belinda Chandra. He argues that Poppy is proof of Time Lord fertility (implying Belinda or the father has Gallifreyan traits, or that Poppy represents a new hybridity). However, the Ranis dismiss Poppy as "impure," exhibiting a fixation on racial purity that aligns with their villainous characterization. They reject the notion of human/Time Lord hybridization, solidifying their ideological opposition to the Doctor's philosophy of integration and love .

#### 2.4 Act III: The Paradox of Poppy
The narrative tension shifts from the macro-threat (Omega) to the micro-threat (the erasure of a child). Poppy is described as an ontological paradox. She is a "memory of a Space Baby," a wish made manifest, and simultaneously "real and not real." The Doctor and Belinda realize that correcting the timeline—undoing the "Wish World"—will likely erase Poppy, as her existence is tied to the divergent reality .

To solve this, "Techy Sue" (a UNIT scientist) constructs a "Schrodinger's Baby Box." This device is designed to insulate Belinda and Poppy from the collapse of the wish reality, theoretically allowing them to survive the transition back to the prime timeline. This subplot underscores the episode's thematic preoccupation with the cost of restoring the status quo .

#### 2.5 Act IV: The Return of Omega and the Bone Palace
The climax unfolds on two fronts. At UNIT, Ruby Sunday and the military forces defend against "enormous skeletons" animated by the reality distortion. Ruby engages Conrad Clark in a psychological confrontation, ultimately neutralizing his threat through empathy rather than violence .

Simultaneously, the Fifteenth Doctor travels to the "Bone Palace" to confront the Ranis and their summoned deity, Omega. The resurrection of Omega goes drastically wrong for the villains. Upon manifesting from the Underverse—now established as his prison, retconning the anti-matter universe of *The Three Doctors*—Omega is depicted as a voracious, uncontrollable force. In a shocking twist, Omega immediately consumes the Archie Panjabi incarnation of The Rani, eating her whole .

Witnessing the death of her other self, the Mrs. Flood incarnation of The Rani realizes the folly of their plan. She utilizes a Time Ring to flee the scene, surviving to potentially return in future stories. The Doctor, left alone with the cosmic threat, utilizes a "special sat nav" device—a piece of technobabble established earlier—to banish Omega back to the Underverse .

#### 2.6 Act V: Restoration and Sacrifice
With Omega defeated, the Doctor instructs Ruby to ask the "Magic Baby" to undo the original wish. Reality resets. Conrad's room transforms back into the TARDIS, and the world returns to normal. However, the tragedy predicted earlier comes to pass. While Poppy initially survives, the laws of the prime universe cannot sustain her. She begins to fade, becoming a "Paradox Baby"—a being who never truly existed in the restored timeline .

The Fifteenth Doctor refuses to accept this loss. He determines that while the "Magic Baby" has become a regular infant, he can use his own life force to cement Poppy's existence. He declares that it will take "an extraordinary amount of power to give reality another nudge and fix the glitch." He chooses to channel his regeneration energy directly into the Time Vortex to rewrite the local timeline .

#### 2.7 The Regeneration
As the Doctor begins the regeneration process, he is visited by a vision of the **Thirteenth Doctor (Jodie Whittaker)**. In a cameo appearance, she advises him that "change is difficult but necessary, and we all have to move on," providing the emotional permission he needs to let go of his current form .

The Fifteenth Doctor releases his energy, saving Poppy (who remains Belinda's daughter, though no longer the Doctor's in this timeline). The regeneration culminates not in the appearance of a new, unknown actor, but in the materialization of **Billie Piper**. The episode ends on this image, with the credits listing her simply as "Introducing Billie Piper," deliberately obscuring whether she is the Sixteenth Doctor, Rose Tyler, or a new entity entirely .

### 3\. Cast and Characters
The ensemble cast for "The Reality War" was extensive, drawing on the series' recent history and its deep lore.

| Character | Actor | Role Breakdown |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Fifteenth Doctor** | **Ncuti Gatwa** | The incumbent Time Lord. This episode marks his final regular appearance. His performance moves from high-energy action hero to a sombre, sacrificial figure willing to trade his life for a child's |
| **Belinda Chandra** | **Varada Sethu** | Companion. Her character arc is heavily criticized for pivoting entirely to motherhood, a shift from her previous independent characterization. She exits the TARDIS to raise Poppy |
| **Ruby Sunday** | **Millie Gibson** | Companion. Ruby serves as the emotional anchor, using her connection to the "Magic Baby" to reset reality. This episode marks her departure from the TARDIS team |
| **Mrs. Flood / The Rani** | **Anita Dobson** | The primary antagonist. Revealed as the classic villain The Rani. Her survival suggests she is intended to be a recurring threat in future seasons |
| **The Rani (Bi-generated)** | **Archie Panjabi** | A younger version of the Rani. Her gruesome death at the hands of Omega serves as the episode's major shock moment regarding the villains |
| **Conrad Clark** | **Jonah Hauer-King** | The human element of the "Unholy Trinity." His storyline is resolved through Ruby's intervention |
| **Omega** | **Nicholas Briggs (Voice)** | The legendary founder of Time Lord society. Portrayed as a kaiju-like monster from the Underverse. This is his first TV appearance since 1983 |
| **The Thirteenth Doctor** | **Jodie Whittaker** | A cameo appearance designed to bridge the regeneration. Whittaker's return was kept secret until broadcast |
| **"The Sixteenth Doctor"** | **Billie Piper** | The result of the regeneration. Her ambiguous credit ("Introducing...") sparked intense fan debate |

**Supporting Cast:**

* **Jemma Redgrave** as Kate Lethbridge-Stewart (UNIT Lead). 
* **Bonnie Langford** as Melanie Bush (Classic Companion/UNIT). 
* **Ruth Madeley** as Shirley Anne Bingham (UNIT Science Advisor). 
* **Yasmin Finney** as Rose Noble (Donna Noble's daughter). 
* **Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps** as Poppy (The Paradox Child). 
* **Steph de Whalley** as Anita Benn (Time Hotel Manager).

### 4\. Critical Analysis and Reception
#### 4.1 Narrative Criticism: The "Exposition Problem"
A recurring critique of "The Reality War" was its reliance on heavy exposition to resolve complex plot threads. Reviewers at *Kabooooom* noted that characters spent significant screen time "explaining things to other characters instead of doing things," a tendency attributed to Russell T Davies' writing style in this era . The complex mechanics of the "Wish World," the "Time Hotel," and the "Underverse" required lengthy dialogue scenes that slowed the narrative momentum.

#### 4.2 The Lore Controversy: Sterility and Bi-Generation
The episode's additions to *Doctor Who* lore were polarizing. The revelation of Time Lord sterility was viewed by long-time fans as a contradiction of the series' history, specifically the "Timeless Child" arc and the Doctor's own mentions of family . Critics argued that making bi-generation the primary method of reproduction was a "hand-wave" that fundamentally altered the biological nature of the species .

Furthermore, the characterization of Belinda Chandra drew ire. Feminist critiques highlighted that her reduction to a "mother figure" driven solely by maternal instinct—after being established as a character resistant to such roles—was "unfortunate" and regressive. Her exit was unfavorably compared to Katarina, a First Doctor companion known for a hasty and poorly written departure .

#### 4.3 Visual Spectacle and Tone
Conversely, the visual ambition of the episode received praise. The realization of the "Bone Palace" and the "Underverse" was cited as evidence of the positive impact of the Disney+ budget. *Pajiba* described the episode as "relentlessly bonkers" and an "enjoyable ride," praising Davies for not "holding back" on the weirdness that defines *Doctor Who*.1 The tone was described as a mix of high camp (The Ranis) and sincere tragedy (The Doctor's sacrifice).

#### 4.4 Ratings and Viewership
The viewership figures for "The Reality War" illustrated the changing landscape of television consumption in 2025\.

* **Overnight:** The episode drew 2.2 million viewers live . 
* **Consolidated (7-Day):** The figure rose to 3.44 million viewers . 
* **Market Share:** It achieved an 18.8% audience share .

While these raw numbers were lower than historical peaks, context is crucial. The episode was the **18th most-watched programme of the week** across all UK channels, and the **2nd most-watched non-soap drama** on the BBC . This data suggests that while linear viewership had declined, *Doctor Who* remained a dominant force in the scripted drama sector.

### 5\. The "Billie Piper" Ending and Future Implications
The final moments of "The Reality War" generated the most significant volume of discourse. The regeneration of Ncuti Gatwa into Billie Piper was a deliberate subversion of audience expectations.

**Theories and Interpretations:**

1. **The Curator/Great Curator Theory:** Some fans speculated that this incarnation represents the Doctor revisiting "old favorite" faces, similar to the Fourth Doctor's return as The Curator. 
2. **The "Rose Tyler" Echo:** Given Piper's history as Rose Tyler, theories abounded that this entity is not the Doctor but a manifestation of the "Bad Wolf" or the TARDIS consciousness taking a familiar form to heal the Doctor. 
3. **The "Valeyard" Inverse:** Others posited she might be a separate entity created from the Doctor's excess regeneration energy, similar to the "Meta-Crisis Doctor" or the Valeyard.

The credit "Introducing Billie Piper" (without "as The Doctor") was analyzed as a strategic move by the BBC to maintain mystery for the upcoming 2026 specials or Season 3 .

**Part II: The Reality War (Literary Series)**

### 1\. Publication and Authorship
Distinct from the *Doctor Who* episode, *The Reality War* is a science fiction novel series written by **Tim C. Taylor**. Published in 2012 by Greyhart Press and CreateSpace, the series comprises two volumes:

1. *The Reality War Book 1: The Slough of Despond* (February 2012) . 
2. *The Reality War Book 2: The City of Destruction* (September 2012) .

### 2\. Plot and Themes
Taylor's series is an allegorical science fiction adventure that explicitly parallels John Bunyan's *The Pilgrim's Progress*. The narrative is set against a temporal conflict initiated in 1992 by a character named Radlan Saravanan.

The central premise involves two rival realities battling for dominance. In this war, the victor's reality becomes "truth," while the loser's reality is erased from existence entirely. The protagonists are described as "mirror images of each other" from these opposing timelines, forced to undertake a spiritual and physical journey through landscapes named after Bunyan's allegorical locations (e.g., The Slough of Despond) .

### 3\. Critical Reception
The book series was well-received within independent science fiction circles. Reviewers praised its "mind-altering twisty tale" and the ethical complexity of its central conflict. The notion that "history will remember only the winner" was explored through a lens that questioned the righteousness of the victors. The series is often cited as a foundational work for Taylor, who would go on to achieve significant success with *The Human Legion* military sci-fi series .

**Conclusion**

"The Reality War" serves as a homonym for two distinct explorations of ontological conflict. In the realm of television, it marks a watershed moment for *Doctor Who*, defining the end of the Fifteenth Doctor's era with controversial lore changes, high-budget spectacle, and a cliffhanger that leverages the franchise's nostalgia. In literature, it represents Tim C. Taylor's allegorical examination of survival and reality. Both works, though separated by medium and magnitude of audience, grapple with the fragility of existence and the lengths to which individuals will go to preserve their version of the truth.

Omega is portrayed as a kaiju-like monster from the Underverse.
This is Omega's first TV appearance since 1983.
Jodie Whittaker made a cameo appearance as The Thirteenth Doctor.
Jodie Whittaker's return as The Thirteenth Doctor was kept secret until broadcast.
Billie Piper is the result of the regeneration.
Billie Piper's ambiguous credit ("Introducing...") sparked intense fan debate.
A recurring critique of "The Reality War" was its reliance on heavy exposition to resolve complex plot threads.

Reviewers at *Kabooooom* noted that characters spent significant screen time "explaining things to other characters instead of doing things," a tendency attributed to Russell T Davies' writing style in this era.
The complex mechanics of the "Wish World," the "Time Hotel," and the "Underverse" required lengthy dialogue scenes that slowed the narrative momentum.
The episode's additions to *Doctor Who* lore were polarizing.
The revelation of Time Lord sterility was viewed by long-time fans as a contradiction of the series' history, specifically the "Timeless Child" arc and the Doctor's own mentions of family.
Critics argued that making bi-generation the primary method of reproduction was a "hand-wave" that fundamentally altered the biological nature of the species.
Furthermore, the characterization of Belinda Chandra drew ire.

Feminist critiques highlighted that Belinda Chandra's reduction to a "mother figure" driven solely by maternal instinct—after being established as a character resistant to such roles—was "unfortunate" and regressive.
Belinda Chandra's exit was unfavorably compared to Katarina, a First Doctor companion known for a hasty and poorly written departure.
Conversely, the visual ambition of the episode received praise.
The realization of the "Bone Palace" and the "Underverse" was cited as evidence of the positive impact of the Disney+ budget.
*Pajiba* described the episode as "relentlessly bonkers" and an "enjoyable ride," praising Davies for not "holding back" on the weirdness that defines *Doctor Who*.
The tone of the episode was described as a mix of high camp (The Ranis) and sincere tragedy (The Doctor's sacrifice).
The viewership figures for "The Reality War" illustrated the changing landscape of television consumption in 2025.
The episode "The Reality War" drew 2.2 million viewers live.
The consolidated (7-Day) viewership figure for "The Reality War" rose to 3.44 million viewers.
The episode "The Reality War" achieved an 18.8% audience share.
While these raw numbers were lower than historical peaks, context is crucial.
The episode "The Reality War" was the 18th most-watched programme of the week across all UK channels.
The episode "The Reality War" was the 2nd most-watched non-soap drama on the BBC.
This data suggests that while linear viewership had declined, *Doctor Who* remained a dominant force in the scripted drama sector.
The final moments of "The Reality War" generated the most significant volume of discourse.
The regeneration of Ncuti Gatwa into Billie Piper was a deliberate subversion of audience expectations.
Some fans speculated that this incarnation represents the Doctor revisiting "old favorite" faces, similar to the Fourth Doctor's return as The Curator.
Given Piper's history as Rose Tyler, theories abounded that this entity is not the Doctor but a manifestation of the "Bad Wolf" or the TARDIS consciousness taking a familiar form to heal the Doctor.
Others posited she might be a separate entity created from the Doctor's excess regeneration energy, similar to the "Meta-Crisis Doctor" or the Valeyard.
The credit "Introducing Billie Piper" (without "as The Doctor") was analyzed as a strategic move by the BBC to maintain mystery for the upcoming 2026 specials or Season 3.
Distinct from the *Doctor Who* episode, *The Reality War* is a science fiction novel series written by Tim C. Taylor.
The *The Reality War* novel series was published in 2012 by Greyhart Press and CreateSpace.
The *The Reality War* novel series comprises two volumes.
*The Reality War Book 1: The Slough of Despond* was published in February 2012.
*The Reality War Book 2: The City of Destruction* was published in September 2012.
Taylor's series is an allegorical science fiction adventure that explicitly parallels John Bunyan's *The Pilgrim's Progress*.
The narrative of Taylor's series is set against a temporal conflict initiated in 1992 by a character named Radlan Saravanan.
The central premise of Taylor's series involves two rival realities battling for dominance.
In this war, the victor's reality becomes "truth," while the loser's reality is erased from existence entirely.
The protagonists of Taylor's series are described as "mirror images of each other" from these opposing timelines.
The protagonists of Taylor's series are forced to undertake a spiritual and physical journey through landscapes named after Bunyan's allegorical locations (e.g., The Slough of Despond).
The book series *The Reality War* was well-received within independent science fiction circles.
Reviewers praised *The Reality War* for its "mind-altering twisty tale" and the ethical complexity of its central conflict.
The notion that "history will remember only the winner" was explored through a lens that questioned the righteousness of the victors.
The series *The Reality War* is often cited as a foundational work for Taylor, who would go on to achieve significant success with *The Human Legion* military sci-fi series.

#### Synopsis

From Book 1:

In 1992, Radlan Saravanan runs a small business out of a Tudor cottage in the sleepy English village of Elstow. But Radlan was born in 2951, and when he falls in love with a local girl, he has to choose between running from his own people and condemning his lover to die.

He makes the wrong choice.

Travelling into the past, falling in love... it turns out he was _meant_ to do these things. He's been manipulated all along, but now he's slipped his handlers, and Time is no longer following the right script. Other versions of history vie for dominance, and our reality is losing.

In 1992, Radlan Saravanan sparked **The Reality War**.

_The Reality War_ is a two-novel series that echoes _The Pilgrim's Progress_ by John Bunyan. It is both a sci-fi action-adventure series, and a spiritual journey made by two people, mirror images of each other from rival realities. It is a side story set in the bestselling Human Legion Universe (Human Legion, Sleeping Legion, Revenge Squad, Chimera Company).

"**The Reality War**" is the eighth and final episode of the [fifteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15") of the British science-fiction television series _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_. Written by [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") and directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai, it is the second of a two-part story alongside the preceding episode, "[Wish World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_World "Wish World")". The episode was released [simultaneously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulcast "Simulcast") on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer"), [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One"), and [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") on 31 May 2025. [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") stars in his final regular appearance as the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor"). [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu") and [Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson") star as his [companions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_(Doctor_Who) "Companion (Doctor Who)"), [Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra") and [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday"), respectively, in their final appearances. Numerous other performers from Gatwa's time on the show reprise their roles. [Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker") also returns as the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor"), while the ending reintroduces [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who previously played [Rose Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler"), to the series when the Doctor [regenerates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_(Doctor_Who) "Regeneration (Doctor Who)").

The episode depicts the Doctor and his allies uniting to combat the threat of [the Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani"), who aims to bring [Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omega_(Doctor_Who) "Omega (Doctor Who)"), the first [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord"), back to the universe to re-create her and the Doctor's home planet [Gallifrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallifrey "Gallifrey") under her rule. The Doctor aims to stop the Rani while also preserving the life of [Poppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poppy_(Doctor_Who) "Poppy (Doctor Who)"), an infant child the Doctor had with Belinda in an altered reality, who will be erased from existence if the Rani's plans succeed. Primary filming took place in 2024, with some re-shoots reportedly taking place into 2025 causing delayed edits to the episode. "The Reality War" was viewed by a total of 3.44 million. It was also given a [limited theatrical release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_theatrical_release "Limited theatrical release") alongside "Wish World". The episode received mixed reviews from critics, who criticised the handling of Belinda's character, the usage of the Rani and Omega as antagonists, the overall plot, and Piper's return, despite some praise for Whittaker's cameo.

As Earth collapses out of reality, [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") is rescued by [Anita Benn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Benn "Anita Benn"), whom he befriended while spending a year with.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Joy-2) She brings him to the [Time Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Hotel_(Doctor_Who) "Time Hotel (Doctor Who)"). He learns [the Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani") put Earth into a [time loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_loop "Time loop") by using a wish from [Conrad Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conrad_Clark "Conrad Clark") and Desiderium, an infant god with the power to transform wishes into reality. The Doctor and Anita use the Time Hotel's doors to restore the memories of his [companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_(Doctor_Who) "Companion (Doctor Who)"), [Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra"), and everyone at [UNIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNIT "UNIT"), while [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday") and other UNIT agents have their memories restored via chip implants.

The Rani and [Mrs. Flood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs._Flood "Mrs. Flood") confront the Doctor, revealing their plan to bring [Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omega_(Doctor_Who) "Omega (Doctor Who)") into the universe and use him as a gene bank to create a new race of [Time Lords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord") under their rule. The Doctor has Belinda take [Poppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poppy_(Doctor_Who) "Poppy (Doctor Who)"), their daughter created in this altered reality, into a special chamber to prevent Poppy being erased once reality is restored to normal. He infiltrates the Rani's palace as Omega - now a massive, skeletal monstrosity - is brought into existence. Omega states he intends to consume all and eats the Rani. Mrs. Flood flees as the Doctor forces Omega back into his prison using the [Vindicator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vindicator_(Doctor_Who) "Vindicator (Doctor Who)"). Ruby breaches the palace to steal Desiderium. Ruby wishes for Conrad to be happy in a new life and for his wish to be undone. The Doctor rejoins her in the TARDIS and makes a wish for Desiderium to no longer grant wishes.

Reality is restored back to normal, though with minor differences. The now human Desiderium is given to Ruby's family, and Anita departs for the Time Hotel, revealing to the Doctor that "the Boss" extends greetings to him. The Doctor and Belinda prepare to depart with Poppy, only for Poppy to be erased with only Ruby remembering her. Ruby persuades the Doctor that Poppy's erasure is a mistake, reminding him of how he saved her as a baby as well.[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-3) In an effort to restore Poppy, the Doctor departs in the TARDIS where, briefly assisted by his [thirteenth incarnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor"), he initiates a [regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_(Doctor_Who) "Regeneration (Doctor Who)") so that the energy of it can be used in conjunction with the time vortex to slightly shift the timeline. The shift results in a timeline where Poppy exists as Belinda's daughter, but not his. After bidding farewell, he departs to begin his next regeneration in the presence of the star of Joy,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Joy-2) appearing to take on a new incarnation resembling former companion [Rose Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler").

"The Reality War" was written by [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-4) After being mentioned in the [first part of the story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_World "Wish World"), the episode re-introduces [Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omega_(Doctor_Who) "Omega (Doctor Who)") to _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_ after last appearing in the programme 42 years earlier.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Omega-5) Davies originally intended to write a new [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord") in place of Omega, but as the script developed he felt that using the already established character was a better fit.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-6)

Davies said that the story wraps up several threads that have been running throughout the Fifteenth Doctor's era, dating back to the 2023 episode "[The Church on Ruby Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_on_Ruby_Road "The Church on Ruby Road")".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-DWM_Preview-7) After warning prior to release that the plot "shakes up the lore of [Gallifrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallifrey "Gallifrey")",[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-8) Davies included an explanation for the concept of "bigeneration"—a twist on the long-time concept of [regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_(Doctor_Who) "Regeneration (Doctor Who)")—that was first seen in "[The Giggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Giggle_(Doctor_Who) "The Giggle (Doctor Who)")" (2023).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-9) He also revealed that he long had the idea of the Doctor falling to his death on a balcony, but never had a resolution for the concept. [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat")'s creation of the Time Hotel for "[Joy to the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_(Doctor_Who) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)")" ultimately provided him that solution as doors from the hotel could open into any location or time period.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Episode_BTS-10)

Despite being two different versions of the same character, the character dynamic between [the Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani") and Mrs Flood were written to have separate personalities, with the former taking credit for their plans while the latter handled much of the physical work.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-11) This dynamic was also further affected once Omega was added, with the Rani seeing Omega as someone worthy of worship.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-12) The [read-through](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read-through "Read-through") of the episode was dedicated to the memory of [Kate O'Mara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_O%27Mara "Kate O'Mara"), who played the original incarnation of [the Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-13)

The episode sees the departure of [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa"), [Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson"), and [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu") in their roles as the [fifteenth incarnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") of [The Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday"), and [Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra"), respectively. While Gatwa insisted it was "always the plan" for him to only spend a short time playing the lead role because of its "physically and emotionally" demanding aspects,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Unleashed-14) comments he initially made about returning for a third series caused the belief that he either departed or was let go from the programme for other reasons such as declining viewing figures, uncertainty over _Doctor Who_'s future with [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") and as a whole, or due to displeasure from executives.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-15) In an interview with _[BBC Breakfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC\_Breakfast "BBC Breakfast")_ on 13 July 2025, Gatwa clarified his statement that he had chosen to quit his role after two series due to the mental and physical toll it was taking on him, but added that he would not rule out returning to the show in the future.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-16)

[Archie Panjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Panjabi "Archie Panjabi") and [Anita Dobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Dobson "Anita Dobson") both portray the Rani in the episode, while [Jonah Hauer-King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hauer-King "Jonah Hauer-King"), [Ruth Madeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Madeley "Ruth Madeley"), [Michelle Greenidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Greenidge "Michelle Greenidge"), Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps, [Jemma Redgrave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jemma_Redgrave "Jemma Redgrave"), [Susan Twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Twist "Susan Twist"), Alexander Devrient, [Bonnie Langford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Langford "Bonnie Langford"), and [Angela Wynter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Wynter "Angela Wynter") reprise their roles as from the previous episode as Conrad Clark, Shirley Bingham, Carla Sunday, Poppy, [Kate Lethbridge-Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Lethbridge-Stewart "Kate Lethbridge-Stewart"), Susan Triad, Colonel Christopher Ibrahim, [Melanie Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanie_Bush "Melanie Bush"), and Cherry Sunday, respectively.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-RT_Cast-17) Aidan Cook also appears as the Vlinx, [Yasmin Finney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasmin_Finney "Yasmin Finney") appears as Rose Noble, and Steph de Whalley reappears as Anita Benn.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-RT_Cast-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-18) Omega was voiced by [Nicholas Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Briggs "Nicholas Briggs"), with the character's physical appearance being handled via [computer generated graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer-generated_imagery "Computer-generated imagery").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Omega-5)

[![Image 3: Jodie Whittaker smiles and wears a white sweatshirt with rainbow stripes](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Jodie_Whittaker_%2852549715171%29.jpg/250px-Jodie_Whittaker_%2852549715171%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jodie_Whittaker_(52549715171).jpg)

[![Image 4: Billie Piper stands in front of a microphone at a convention](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Billie_Piper_at_Brussels_Comic_Con_2019_12-08-40_ILCE-6500_DSC00364_DxO_%2846561728515%29.jpg/250px-Billie_Piper_at_Brussels_Comic_Con_2019_12-08-40_ILCE-6500_DSC00364_DxO_%2846561728515%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Billie_Piper_at_Brussels_Comic_Con_2019_12-08-40_ILCE-6500_DSC00364_DxO_(46561728515).jpg)

[Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker") reprised her role as the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor"), marking her first reappearance since "[The Power of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Power_of_the_Doctor "The Power of the Doctor")" (2022).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-19) Whittaker's name was disguised as "Petrol" on the [daily call sheets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_call_sheet "Daily call sheet") to hide her return prior to filming, with the Fifteenth Doctor also named as "Clive" on Whittaker's copy of the script.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Unleashed-14) Whittaker said it was special to be part of a regeneration episode with another performer, as she had filmed her regeneration scenes independently of both her predecessor, [Peter Capaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Capaldi "Peter Capaldi"), and successor, [David Tennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tennant "David Tennant").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Episode_BTS-10)

Davies said that he wanted to include a scene where the Thirteenth and Fifteenth Doctors met because he felt like there was a missing link between the two due to the casting of Tennant as the [Fourteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor"). Tight filming schedules also required Whittaker to be flown in for her one day on set as she was abroad while recording was underway.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-20) In "The Reality War", Whittaker wore a wig as her hair was now long and brown, rather than the short blonde style her character previously had.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Unleashed-14)

[Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper") also returned to _Doctor Who_ in this episode when the Fifteenth Doctor regenerates into a character portrayed by her at the end of the episode,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-21) after last appearing in the 2013 fiftieth anniversary special, "[The Day of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Day_of_the_Doctor "The Day of the Doctor")".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-22) While Piper's official role remains undisclosed, with the closing credits merely reading "introducing Billie Piper",[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-23) some sources assumed her to be portraying the sixteenth incarnation of the Doctor.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-24)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-25) According to Piper, she was approached in a "very last minute" capacity.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-26)

### Filming and post-production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Reality_War&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Filming and post-production")]

"The Reality War" was directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-27) Gatwa's action sequences on a [personal transporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_transporter "Personal transporter") were filmed in front of a [green screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_screen "Green screen"). A scene where Anita opens a door to see the Third Doctor and the [Daleks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daleks "Daleks") was originally intended to be created using archive footage from the 1972 _Doctor Who_ serial _[Day of the Daleks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day\_of\_the\_Daleks "Day of the Daleks")_. However, Pillai came up with the idea to use a practical Dalek prop in the foreground for a better connection between the two stories.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Episode_BTS-10) The scene with Omega required shooting the scene in a wider shot to accommodate Omega's size, with Panjabi being strung on wires to allow Omega to pick her up.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-Episode_BTS-10)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") on series fifteen finished in May 2024,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-28)[Post-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-production "Post-production") on the episode was still incomplete by April 2025, something that Davies attributed to the large number of [visual effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects "Visual effects") that the episode contained. Composer [Murray Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_Gold "Murray Gold") also had [appendicitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendicitis "Appendicitis"), further delaying the episode. Davies hoped to have the final edit approved by 17 April.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-DWM_Preview-7)

[![Image 5: Attendees are dancing at a birthday party](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/43/The_Reality_War_Deleted_Scene.jpg/250px-The_Reality_War_Deleted_Scene.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Reality_War_Deleted_Scene.jpg)

In this promotional photo for the episode released by [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+"), [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor") and [Belinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra") can be seen at a party. This [deleted scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deleted_scene "Deleted scene") was removed from the [final cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_cut_privilege "Final cut privilege") of the episode.

Additional filming reportedly took place in February 2025. The additional scenes, which comprised a third of the episode, were speculated to have been necessary to allow Gatwa to leave the series, and were also rumoured to include the appearance of Whittaker and Piper. Additionally, some scenes were supposedly removed from the original [final cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_cut_privilege "Final cut privilege"), one of which would have introduced Archie Lal as Belinda's father Hari.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-29)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-IGN_Deleted-30)

Information about another [deleted scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deleted_scene "Deleted scene") arose from a promotional photo released by Disney+ that featured the Doctor and Belinda dancing at a party, a segment that would have been the final moments and ultimately never appeared in the episode. [Susan Foreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Foreman "Susan Foreman"), a character portrayed by [Carole Ann Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carole_Ann_Ford "Carole Ann Ford"), who was re-introduced to the programme after a forty year absence as the Doctor's granddaughter two episodes prior, and Ruby would also have allegedly been present in this final scene. Ford's appearance would have also resulted in a [cliffhanger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliffhanger "Cliffhanger") for the [next series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_16 "Doctor Who series 16").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-31)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-IGN_Deleted-30) Comments made on a [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") account run by Mavanga-Phipps's mother suggested that the original plot would have also revealed Poppy to actually be the Doctor's daughter and Susan's mother.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-IGN_Deleted-30)

Ford later confirmed the existence of the cut scene in response to an interview question about whether Susan knew her mother, stating: "You didn’t see the episode which was to sort of introduce my coming back, where I was holding hands with a [...] beautiful little tiny black child, three years old. And we were watching through the window somewhere where the audience wasn’t supposed to know where we supposed to be. And we were watching by newly-embodied grandfather, who was now Ncuti [Gatwa], and watching him have a wonderful time singing and dancing in a party in a shop opposite where we were."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-32)

No [advanced screenings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preview_screening "Preview screening") for the press were held in order to keep the ending moments of the episode confidential.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-43) "The Reality War" was released [simultaneously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simulcast "Simulcast") on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") and [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") in the United Kingdom, and on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") in the United States,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-44) at 6:50 p.m. [British Summer Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Summer_Time "British Summer Time") (BST) and 10:50 a.m. [Pacific Daylight Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Daylight_Time "Pacific Daylight Time"), respectively, on 31 May 2025.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-45) It is the first global simulcast of a _Doctor Who_ episode since "The Church on Ruby Road".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-DWM_Preview-7) With a total runtime of 70 minutes, it is the longest _Doctor Who_ episode of the [fifteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-46) The episode, along with the story's first part, "Wish World", received a simultaneous [limited theatrical release](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_theatrical_release "Limited theatrical release") in cinemas in the UK and Ireland.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-47)

The episode received overnight viewing figures of 2.2 million, the second highest of the day.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-48) This increased to 3.44 million after seven days.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-49) "Wish World" and "The Reality War" brought in £381,725, ranking second for event screenings of the day at the UK box office, only behind _[Peppa Meets the Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peppa\_Meets\_the\_Baby "Peppa Meets the Baby")_.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-50)

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 54% of 13 critics' reviews are positive.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-RT-33) Writing for _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_, Will Salmon highlighted the episode's ambitious scope, Jodie Whittaker's cameo and the emotional resonance of certain scenes, noting specifically the "touching send-off for Ncuti Gatwa's Doctor".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-GR+-37) Salmon criticised the handling of Belinda's character arc, believing that having her become a mother caused her arc to be begin and end with "toxic men"; as well as the inclusion of Omega and the Rani, which he found underwhelming.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-GR+-37) Stefan Mohamed from _[Den of Geek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Den\_of\_Geek "Den of Geek")_ criticised the sidelining of Belinda in the chamber, noting that she "functionally stops existing as a narrative presence"; while acknowledging the surprise elements like Gatwa's unexpected regeneration, Mohamed disliked the episode's storytelling choices and felt that Belinda's character arc was ultimately wasted and overshadowed by Ruby's.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-51)

Robert Anderson from _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ found the episode to be "overstuffed", believing the episode's villains lacking in presence, while also disliking the end of Belinda's arc within the series, feeling that it was too rushed rather than a poor concept. Anderson, however, did highlight Whittaker's brief appearance as the Thirteenth Doctor.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-IGN-39) Michael Hogan, writing for _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Daily\_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_, criticised the episode's narrative, which he felt had too many characters. He disliked Poppy's plotline as he felt it was hard to care about, and the usage of Omega as an antagonist. However, he praised Panjabi's performance as the Rani.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-52) Stephen Kelly of _[i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_(newspaper) "I (newspaper)")_ criticised the subplot involving Poppy and the usage of Belinda, though he praised Whittaker's cameo.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-auto-38) Isobel Lewis of _[The A.V. Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_A.V.\_Club "The A.V. Club")_ similarly criticised several aspects of the "incredibly rushed" episode, including the usage of Panjabi's Rani and Omega, and Conrad's story conclusion.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-auto1-34) Jennifer Zhan of [Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(magazine) "Vulture (magazine)") criticised the usage of the Rani and Omega, as well as Conrad and Belinda's story arc conclusions.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-auto2-42) Piper's return was met with criticism for relying too much on [nostalgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nostalgia "Nostalgia") through the use of previous cast members.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War#cite_note-53)

6.title: DOCTOR WHO: THE REALITY WAR [Review]
6.description: The Reality War, much like Doctor Who Series 2, is conflicted and troubling, despite some brilliant moments.
6.content:
It occurs to me with this, the final episode of Doctor Who Series 2, why I’ve had such a hard time reviewing most of the episodes this season. There’s too much exposition!

When writing a review, it’s my job to offer context for the story without spoiling the plot. That’s been rather difficult when so many of the stories this season were largely made up of the characters explaining things to other characters instead of doing things. Granted, that’s part and parcel of Doctor Who, which famously turned “I’ll explain later…” into a mantra. But Russell T Davies really went overboard with it this time around.

![Image 1: Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in The Reality War](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/ncuti-gatwa-as-the-doctor-in-the-reality-war.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

I can say this much. Many of the seemingly random elements I noted when discussing [Wish World](https://kabooooom.com/2025/05/24/doctor-who-wish-world-review/) are explained here. Unfortunately, there is also a lot that will make various Classic Who fans alternatively punch the air in triumph or groan in despair. Worse yet, something happens in this episode that makes the Doctor’s torturing a terrorist in [The Interstellar Song Contest](https://kabooooom.com/2025/05/17/doctor-who-the-interstellar-song-contest-review/) seem far worse by comparison if any kind of thought is applied to it.

Nothing but SPOILERS beyond this image kids.

![Image 2: Doctor Who Series 2 Ncuti Gatwa and Varada Sethu](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/doctor-who-series-2-ncuti-gatwa-and-varada-sethu.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

When last we left off, The Doctor was falling to certain death after learning The Ranis’ plan; to find the lost Time Lord founder, Omega. In Classic Who, Omega was said to be trapped in the anti-matter universe. This has been retconned to make him a prisoner of the Underverse – the same weird realm under the material plane which The Toymaker calls home.

Thankfully, one of The Doctor’s good deeds pays off and he is saved by Anita; the hotel manager he helped give a new lease on life during [Joy To The World](https://kabooooom.com/2024/12/26/doctor-who-joy-to-the-world-review/). Now Manager of the Time Hotel, Anita has been watching out for the Time Lord and gave him an exit when he most needed it. She also helps him to reawaken his friends at UNIT by literally holding open the door to reality. Unfortunately, this still leaves the problem of how to save a child – the last Time Lord child – once reality asserts itself once The Ranis are defeated.

![Image 3: Doctor Who The Reality War Doctor and Anita](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/doctor-who-the-reality-war-doctor-and-anita.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

I don’t need to discuss the action of this episode. We know that The Doctor will win, if not without cost, and Omega will be driven back to the realm of myth. The problem is that Russell T. Davies drops a lot of lore and the explanations create more problems than they solve.

Vexingly, they also undo some of the best stories of Davies first run as showrunner. However, thinking on it, the stories he undoes are mostly written by Steven Moffatt. This may not be a coincidence given the random slam of the most popular New Who stories back in [Lux](https://kabooooom.com/2025/04/19/doctor-who-lux-review/). But I digress.

![Image 4: UNIT in Doctor Who The Reality War](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/unit-in-doctor-who-the-reality-war.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

The biggest revelation here is that Time Lords are confirmed to be unfertile. There is no such thing as a Time Lord child, we are told. That tiny cheer you heard was every New Adventures reader rejoicing that [Lungbarrow](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Lungbarrow_(novel)) is now somewhat closer to being canon. The slightly louder “What?” you heard was every New Who fan shouting “Since When?” and wondering how that reconciles the Ninth Doctor’s talk about having been a father and grandfather, the Tenth Doctor counting every child lost on Gallifrey during the Time War, The Master being driven mad as a child while starring into the Time Vortex, the entire Timeless Child story arc, and the existence of Susan, the Doctor’s granddaughter.

Oh! And bigeneration, which was supposed to be a big Time Lord myth? That’s how Time Lords reproduce now. (Sorry Lungbarrow fans!)

Most of this can be hand-waved as a change in continuity thanks to all the wibbly-wobbly timey-wimey nonsense that happened during Flux or when The Doctor broke into the Underverse. This wouldn’t be the first time Doctor Who contradicted a large chunk of its history for the sake of one story. The problem is that the payoff isn’t really worth it.

![Image 5: Belinda Chandra and Poppy in Doctor Who The Reality War](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/belinda-chandra-and-poppy-in-doctor-who-the-reality-war.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

I commented before about how Varada Sethu had little to do in Wish World beyond scream about her baby. That issue is cranked up to 11 in The Reality War, as Belinda Chandra has her memories of who she really is restored. Yet she remains entirely focused on saving Poppy, the child born of her and John Smith’s marriage on Wish World. Granting that motherhood does tend to change most women’s priorities, not all women have an instant maternal instinct.

Belinda never got much characterization beyond “nurse,” “wants to go home,” and “low tolerance for men’s bullshit, including The Doctor.” Nothing in her six stories before this seemed to hint at her wanting to be a mom. It gets even worse when you consider that Belinda’s involvement in The Doctor’s life was indirectly set up by her sexist high school boyfriend. Her entire arc was defined by her not wanting to become a housewife/brood mare to some man. And yet, The Doctor rewrites reality so she becomes a mother, just so that Poppy can survive. The implications are unfortunate.

![Image 6: The Thirteenth and Fifteenth Doctors in Doctor Who.](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/the-thirteenth-and-fifteenth-doctors-in-doctor-who.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

Facilitating this requires the Doctor to expend the last of the life energy for this incarnation. This leads to a surprisingly good scene, as The Thirteenth Doctor suddenly shows up in The TARDIS to deliver some words of encouragement. Specifically, about how change is difficult but necessary, and we all have to move on.

Jodie Whittaker is a marvel in this scene and it pretty much proves that she could have been a fantastic Doctor with better writing. Indeed, it makes one wish that we could have had two Doctors to fight the two Ranis. Alas, the magic of this scene is completely undercut by the ending and Ncuti Gatwa’s surprise regeneration into Billie Piper.

![Image 7: Billie Piper in Doctor Who The Reality War](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/billie-piper-in-doctor-who-the-reality-war.jpg?w=720)

(Image Source: BBC)

Don’t I mean the Sixteenth Doctor? No, because the credits say “And Introducing Billie Piper.” They do not credit her as The Doctor. This opens up the door to all manner of speculation as to what this may mean. Has an older and wiser Rose Tyler manifested into The TARDIS from the other universe? It this The Moment showing up to try and fix all the nonsense and establish a new status quo? Or is it literally Billie Piper playing Billie Piper in the Whoniverse? All are possibilities and equally likely at this point.

And yes, the irony of us getting Billie Piper returning to Doctor Who after a beautiful speech about moving on and not getting caught up in the past is another “What?” moment for me. I have mixed feelings, however, for while I love Piper as an actress, Rose Tyler as a character, and The Moment as a concept, I fear that her return means more of the show looking backward instead of forward. Particularly if Russell T. Davies remains as showrunner.

All in all, I think the good elements of The Reality War balance out the bad. That does not mitigate the problems, however, like Belinda Chandra getting what must be the single worst companion exit since Katarina shot herself into space in The First Doctor era. Still, like most of this season, it could have been far worse, yet should have been much better.

![Image 8: Three blue zeros in the darkness](https://kabooooom.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/9906a-3-5.png)

===============

[‘Doctor Who’ Finale Recap: Doctor Whaaaaat?! ============================================](https://www.pajiba.com/tv_reviews/doctor-who-recap-season-15-finale-the-reality-war-billie-piper-ncuti-gatwa.php)
By [Hannah Sole](https://www.pajiba.com/staff/hannah-sole.php) | [TV](https://www.pajiba.com/tv_reviews/) | June 1, 2025

![Image 5: doctor-who-regeneration.png](https://www.pajiba.com/assets_c/2025/06/doctor-who-regeneration-thumb-700x355-270903.png)

**Header Image Source:** BBC 

**Previously, on _Doctor Who_:** The Two Ranis and their pet Conrad used a magic baby to create a reality-splitting dystopia in order to [bring back Omega](https://www.pajiba.com/tv_reviews/doctor-who-recap-season-15-episode-7-wish-world.php) from the Underverse, and that is absolutely a sentence I never thought I would write.

**This week:** Reality breaks and then so does the internet. Please, please, please watch it before I spoil the heck out of it in 3, 2, I’m not kidding, **spoilers are coming** and they are doozies, 1…

![Image 6: doctor who reality war 2.png](https://www.pajiba.com/assets_c/2025/06/doctor%20who%20reality%20war%202-thumb-700xauto-270901.png)

‘The Reality War’ is relentlessly bonkers and so chock-full of ‘what the chuff’ moments that you think you’ve seen everything, and then another one pops up to knock you down again. If this is Russell T Davies campaigning for a new series with Disney+ money, he’s not holding back. Does it stand up to scrutiny? Well, no, not really. Is it an enjoyable ride? Sure. It’s a loving tour of Fifteen’s time in the Whoniverse, building up to the realisation that _this is it_, and our fabulous Fifteen is bidding farewell. But I am jumping ahead.

Fifteen’s saved from plummeting to the ground by Anita and the Time Hotel, from the last Christmas special. The Time Hotel exists in a kind of interdimensional ‘real time’ future space and can break the Wish World’s hold on the mind. Fifteen and Anita open more doors into UNIT, and everyone inside snaps out of it thanks to the cross-draught. Ruby, Melanie, and Shirley are summoned, Rose rematerializes (Donna’s daughter Rose, not Rose Tyler, that would make no sense, right?) too. Melanie seems to stop for a perm on the way. The Two Ranis pay UNIT a visit and do some more timesplaining about their plan. They want to use Omega to rebuild the Time Lord race because all Gallifreyans are sterile now. Fifteen’s like, uh, Poppy’s real. The Ranis aren’t into human / Time Lord babies though and then everyone seems surprised that a villain has gross ideas about racial purity.

The Poppy problem is where this gets unwieldy. Poppy is real and not real, a memory of a Space Baby, and a wish, and the Doctor’s baby and not the Doctor’s baby. Undoing Wish World might or might not undo Poppy. Fifteen and Belinda can’t risk it, and Techy Sue builds them a Schrodinger’s Baby Box to try to keep Belinda and Poppy safe while everyone else goes to stop the Ranis.

It’s surprisingly easy to stop the Ranis after all that. UNIT fights the enormous skeletons, Ruby has a kinder confrontation with Conrad [than he deserves](https://www.pajiba.com/tv_reviews/doctor-who-recap-season-15-episode-4-lucky-day-conrad-sucks.php), and Fifteen scoots on up to the bone palace for a chat with the Ranis. When Omega shows up, he’s a huge monster and immediately eats The Rani, while Mrs Flood nopes out with a _Two Ronnies_ joke. You’d never catch me doing something so cheesy. [Cough](https://www.pajiba.com/tv_reviews/doctor-who-recap-season-15-episode-6-who-is-the-rani.php). Fifteen blasts Omega back to the Underverse with his special sat nav.

Ruby asks Magic Baby to undo the wish, and everything goes back to normal. Almost. Conrad’s room turns back into the TARDIS. Fifteen wishes for an end to wishes, and just like that, Magic Baby is just a regular baby. Poppy survives and then she fades away and Ruby’s the only one who remembers her. When Fifteen finally realises that fixing the world cost the life of a child, his child no less, he promises to fix it, knowing that it would take an extraordinary amount of power to give reality another nudge and fix the glitch. Regeneration energy into the vortex, in fact. At that moment, Thirteen pops up for a visit to try and talk him out of it, and then give him some advice to do it more efficiently. It’s a lovely moment between them, and a wonderful surprise.

He’s got a few moments to see if it worked, and that’s when he discovers that he has brought Poppy back, but she’s not his. In this new reality, Belinda’s been talking about Poppy the whole time, and desperate to get back to her. Fifteen would have done this for any child, so it’s still on brand, but Poppy is a Paradox Baby, and it feels like a sad twist. Back on the TARDIS, he stands at the door, leaning out into space, to regenerate with Joy from the Christmas special shining on him to keep him company, and go out with a smile on his face like Thirteen recommended. Farewell, Ncuti Gatwa, you wonderful and beautiful Doctor; we’ll miss that warmth, that energy, and that smile.

I was already applauding RTD for managing to do a surprise regeneration because having this unspoiled was fantastic, and we were all squinting at that regeneration light trying to see who was joining the cast, when there was a piercing sound, as if thousands of Whovians had gasped and then called for their fainting couches. BILLIE PIPER! WHAT? _WHAAAAAT?!_

![Image 7: doctor who billie piper.png](https://www.pajiba.com/assets_c/2025/06/doctor%20who%20billie%20piper-thumb-700xauto-270899.png)

I have a lot of questions, and only half of them are _WHAT?_ Are we in a parallel dimension now? When did the Time Lords go sterile? What was with the clips of Susan? Why does Ruby always remember things that other people don’t? How come Belinda’s daughter is the spitting image of a Space Baby she never met? Who’s the boss of the Time Hotel? How come Ruby’s hair looks different after Poppy disappears? RTD magically dodges all of those questions by hurling a zinger in the closing seconds and dropping his mic. _Cancel this, bitches._ Is Billie officially Sixteen? Is she here for a few specials? She’s not listed as The Doctor in the closing credits so she might be a parallel universe Doctor. Is this what The Moment meant when she said the Bad Wolf face was from the Doctor’s past or maybe his future? Is this nostalgia-baiting? Is she going to seek out Fourteen and make things very confusing? Take him on the world’s most awkward double date with Rose and Ten-Too?

Fetch my smelling salts; I need a lie down. Timey-wimey, going strong.

So it turns out [my Glitch theory](https://www.pajiba.com/tv_reviews/doctor-who-recap-season-15-episode-3-the-well.php) was perhaps a little generous and maybe those glitches were not intentional, but there are official and intentional glitches all over the shop now, so that kind of counts. We’ll wait to see what happens with _Doctor Who_, and see how and when it will return. In the meantime, we have a UNIT spin-off to look forward to!

Murray Gold Confirms New Doctor Who Soundtracks (Including Series 10) Are Coming Soon!
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1: Murray Gold Confirms New Doctor Who Soundtracks (Including Series 10) Are Coming Soon!](https://thedoctorwhocompanion.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Series-10-12th-Twelfth-Peter-Capaldi-Pearl-Mackie-Bill-Potts-Nardole-Matt-Lucas-TARDIS.jpg)

*    Posted On: [21 June 2025](https://thedoctorwhocompanion.com/2025/06/21/murray-gold-confirms-new-doctor-who-soundtracks-including-series-10-are-coming-soon/)
*    Posted By: [Philip Bates](https://thedoctorwhocompanion.com/author/prbates36/)
*    Comments: [0](https://thedoctorwhocompanion.com/2025/06/21/murray-gold-confirms-new-doctor-who-soundtracks-including-series-10-are-coming-soon/)

_Doctor Who_ composer, Murray Gold, has confirmed that he’s working on four soundtracks, covering the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Doctors’ eras, as well as Series 10, and they should be coming relatively soon!

The Series 10 soundtrack, a score for Peter Capaldi’s last season as the Twelfth Doctor with Pearl Mackie as Bill Potts and Matt Lucas as Nardole, was left in limbo when Gold left the programme. But speaking at the _Doctor Who Appreciation Society_‘s _20 Years On_ event which celebrated twenty years of 21st Century _Doctor Who_, Murray confirmed that he’s working on the soundtrack again now.

The main issue with the soundtracks is apparently the volume of material available, i.e. how to slim down the scores and distil them into the essence of each series.

The four soundtracks are: Series 10; the 60th anniversary specials from _The Star Beast_ to _The Giggle_; and the Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) era, comprised of Series 14 and 15 (or Season 1 and 2 as some call them).

The Series 10 soundtrack has become something of a running joke, given that it was the only one back then not to be released and by now, it’s for a series that was broadcast in 2017. As [BlogtorWho](https://www.blogtorwho.com/four-new-doctor-who-soundtracks-on-the-way/) notes, there’s even a Twitter/X account that charts all the things that have been released or that have happened before the Series 10 soundtrack is released…

As someone who loves Bill Potts’ theme, I’d love to get my hands on the music for the series!

With the show seemingly in hiatus right now, we can see the BBC needing to put out a lot of merchandise to keep interest alive, so these soundtracks are just the ticket.
