7.content:
\[usr 2.5\]

After a typically hectic setup in “[Wish World](https://www.framerated.co.uk/doctor-who-wish-world/)”, where copious ideas were thrown together with little to no cohesion and logic, the Series 15 finale has arrived. “The Reality War” was a better half of this two-part story, if only because it didn’t have such ridiculous heavy-lifting to do, so writer Russell T. Davies could instead focus on the action and in trying to resolve matters. And while many of the resolutions didn’t entirely work for me, enough did that it was at least mostly inoffensively slapdash.

The huge problem with “The Reality War” is how everything notable about it was thrown into a denouement that took up half the runtime. The machinations of the Rani (Archie Panjabi) ultimately amounted to depressingly little of real value, as she was mostly a bystander to an ‘armed skyscraper vs skeleton monsters’ battle between The Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa), UNIT, and Reality as it managed to reassert itself once Ruby (Millie Gibson) kidnapped the infant ‘God of Wishes’ being held by her toxic ex-boyfriend Conrad (Jonah Hauer-King). The latter was also an afterthought, getting almost nothing to do, although I appreciated the story giving Ruby the agency in his defeat.

We know RTD loves a rushed and easy-fix ending (of the kind a six-year-old might come up with for their action figures), so reversing everything by having a companion ‘wish it so’ was the worst example we’ve seen of this, but at least the story had revolved around magic. The threat of Omega, the first Time Lord trapped in the Underverse, ultimately amounted to very little too—as he was revealed to be a skeletal skin for the show’s ‘Sutekh’ CGI asset, ready for The Doctor to blast into Hell with an improvised ray gun minutes after Omega unceremoniously gobbled up the Rani. The original Rani, Mrs Flood (Anita Dobson), managed to evade capture thanks to a Time Bracelet, so will presumably reappear at some point, but it was a _monumental_ let-down for poor Panjabi in this role. It was also a shame Omega didn’t mention the fact The Doctor is the ‘Timeless Child’ (he would know) and arguably of more standing in Time Lord society than he is, or is this also being quietly swept under the carpet now? It’s hard to keep up, or know what’s definitely foundational lore or a bit of whimsy we’ve collectively agreed to ignore.

![Image 1](https://www.framerated.co.uk/frwpcontent/uploads/2025/06/140BbyMhXe8dWbemtxK11Eg.jpg)

The crazy thing about “The Reality War” is that once everything was over and events started moving to a quiet conclusion, what felt like the denouement suddenly stretched to an extra half-hour. The loose end that provided this extra material was Poppy, the baby girl The Doctor fathered with Belinda (Varada Sethu) while they were inside the ‘wish world’ as a married couple. Hoping to avoid Poppy vanishing when things reverted to normal, The Doctor stowed her in a ‘Zero Box’ that UNIT had lying around, with Belinda agreeing to be her guardian for all eternity if it came to that. (They didn’t even give her some books or a Sudoku to do?) Unfortunately, this meant Bel practically sat out the finale, and it felt ridiculous for a new companion to have such little impact on a series climax.

Nevertheless, after the dust settled, it seemed like Poppy had managed to survive the wish reversal process, until reality slowly reasserted itself and only Ruby noticed everyone gradually forgetting about The Doctor’s young daughter. The episode acknowledged it had no explanation for why Ruby is able to know if things aren’t as they seem, which is either a good thing because it’s refreshingly honest, or a bad thing because it’s acknowledging one key aspect of the story had no real answer. Regardless, Ruby eventually convinces The Doctor that his daughter did once exist, which triggered what felt like a mini-episode. And it felt so unnecessary because they could have just had Poppy’s lineage tweaked once reality returned, rather than have The Doctor accept a surprise mission to force this to happen himself—by blasting some of his regeneration energy into the Time Vortex of the TARDIS, which did the trick for… reasons. If in doubt, make an explosion. And can Time Lords just choose to regenerate now if they need to alter reality?

One of the massive talking points was the unexpected return of the Thirteenth Doctor (Jodie Whittaker) to give Fifteen a pep talk in the TARDIS, for hazy reasons. But it was surprisingly fun to see Jodie back in the role, despite her own run being a huge flop in my eyes, maybe because she’s at least a bit quirky and I miss that core element of The Doctor from Ncuti Gatwa—who was always too well-balanced, confident, and cool for my taste. Maybe that was the point, as the baggage of past Doctors was removed from him, but it shouldn’t alter the fundamental personality of The Doctor being peculiar and quirky. Confidence and coolness is fine, but there was never a feeling Fifteen was an _alien_.

Ultimately, there wasn’t enough emotional impact in what they were trying to achieve at the end, with The Doctor using his regeneration energy to somehow nudge the TARDIS into a parallel universe where Poppy still exists, but was fathered by another man. I see what the intention was, but it failed for me. We didn’t have enough time with The Doctor as a father for his loss to truly register, and it always felt ‘icky’ to me that he slept with a companion who was effectively “brainwashed” to think they were a happily married couple by a wish-giving deity.

![Image 2](https://www.framerated.co.uk/frwpcontent/uploads/2025/06/181fYmXg9NNXKhvFJWfgnNg.jpg)

Then, as hotly rumoured, Ncuti Gatwa regenerated. Thankfully, the bi-generation concept appears to have been quietly set aside. Such moments are pivotal in the history of _Doctor Who_, but I have to say it was horrendously handled here. Most Doctors make a noble sacrifice or have a thrilling moment before they are fatally injured and forced to regenerate, so the quieter and more peculiar reason with Poppy just did not land.

I have read rumours that Ncuti Gatwa was not happy and wanted to leave sooner than expected, or that BBC bosses have been unhappy with the show’s ratings and encouraged RTD to find a different actor (not helped by Gatwa refusing to appear on Eurovision for political reasons), but who knows what the truth is. Maybe it will come out one day, like when Christopher Eccleston started to admit RTD and the producers were terrible people to work for. But it is definitely strange to only hire a new actor for two years, when three is the new norm, and often with longer gaps of time between each run so it feels like the actor had a longer run with the part. For example: Whittaker was announced in 2017 and left in 2023. _Six_ years as The Doctor, but she only appeared in three series and three specials.

Of course, the biggest talking point of the episode is who the Fifteenth Doctor turned into in those final moments. I had read a rumour this was going to happen earlier in the morning, and I did not give it any credence because it sounded like such a ludicrous idea dreamed up by fans… but, good heavens, it was true. Ncuti Gatwa regenerated into Billie Piper, who played the Ninth and Tenth Doctor’s companion Rose back when RTD revived the series in 2005.

Of course, there is a precedent for The Doctor to reuse an “old face”, which is how we had David Tennant return as the Fourteenth incarnation for the 60th anniversary specials, and Peter Capaldi’s Tenth Doctor “borrowed” his appearance from a Roman character Capaldi had previously played on the show before… so the lore is established to support the idea The Doctor can look like someone we are familiar with… but… _Billie Piper_?

![Image 3](https://www.framerated.co.uk/frwpcontent/uploads/2025/06/1oTrGTOTwPc5Rsl9TapMaKA.jpg)

Are we serious? I like Billie Piper. She was well-cast as a companion 20 years ago, but she doesn’t strike me as an actress who fits the part of The Doctor—not at all. And, on a deeper level, it seems like a severe lack of imagination from RTD to cast one of his old pals again, after doing the same thing just a few years ago with Tennant. Aren’t there any young actors who could play The Doctor and get a big break doing it? Where’s the next Matt Smith? And does it bode well for the future of _Doctor Who_ that _two_ incarnations out of the past three have been actors who already appeared on the show in main roles? Do we need to bait fan nostalgia like this, twice? Is stunt-casting now the only way to make audiences stick around, out of sheer curiosity?

_Doctor Who_ should be a forward-facing and progressive show, with refreshment and rejuvenation literally baked into its DNA. We should have fresh voices and faces every three years to keep things lively and different. It was already a disappointment to get RTD back again as showrunner, but I can understand the thinking after Chris Chibnall’s era failed to spark and the BBC needed a safe pair of hands, and the surprise return of David Tennant could be put down to anniversary hijinks… but to once again return to the past like this feels silly and desperate. Maybe Karen Gillan could be next, or bring back Jodie Whittaker for another go? What’s Peter Capaldi up to now? Is Jenna Coleman’s career on the rocks enough to tempt her back? Can Tennant make it a hat-trick? Just keep recycling the past few decades rather than carve a path into the future.

I’m sure some will love the idea. It’s a silly show which has only become sillier in recent times with the dominance of magic over any semblance of proper sci-fi. In some ways the ground’s been laid for left-field, backwards-facing ideas like this, but do people really _want_ Billie Piper to play The Doctor?

Well, let’s see what happens. There are doubts Disney want to continue co-producing the show because it hasn’t been the hit they expected, which is astonishing to me, as it’s still one of the most talked-about sci-fi shows around and surely appeals to the family-friendly Disney+ demographic. If the entire world getting big-budget _Doctor Who_ episodes hours before the UK doesn’t move the dial in terms of ratings, maybe the brand’s in a worse state than we thought right now.

And spare a thought for the late Fifteenth Doctor, who never even glimpsed a Dalek or Cyberman…

11.title: "The Reality War" - 'Doctor Who' Season 2 Finale: Full Cast, Synopsis & Runtime | Popped
11.description: Doctor Who Season 2 concludes with “The Reality War” – a dramatic 66-minute finale featuring the return of The Rani, a full cast list, BBC One air time, and Disney+ release info.
11.content:
_**The Reality War**_ is coming. After weeks of cryptic dialogue and teasing glimpses, **_[Doctor Who](https://poppednews.com/doctor-who/)_** has finally pulled back the curtain on one of its most mysterious new figures — and the twist is bigger than anyone expected. In a dramatic reveal during **_[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/17/doctor-who-season-2-the-interstellar-song-contest-review/)_**, **Anita Dobson’s** enigmatic Mrs Flood was unveiled as none other than the Rani — a classic villain from the show’s storied past, now reimagined in a bi-generated twist that introduces Emmy Award-winner **Archie Panjabi** into the mix. In the first part of the _Doctor Who_ Season 2 finale, titled **_Wish World_**, releasing this week, traps are sprung and old enemies unite as the Doctor (**Ncuti Gatwa**) and Belinda (**Varada Sethu**) finally arrive home to find a very different world. Can the Doctor see the truth before midnight arrives? Following on from an inevitable cliffhanger, the final part, titled _The Reality War,_ will conclude the season, tying up loose ends – but what is the synopsis and who will appear?

![Image 1: tbTwYCVI o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/tbTwYCVI_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

The **[official BBC synopsis](https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002d3lr)** for the _Doctor Who_ Season 2 finale, titled “The Reality War” reads:

> _Battle rages across the skies as the Unholy Trinity unleash their deadly ambition. The Doctor, Belinda and Ruby have to risk everything in the quest to save one innocent life._

_The Reality War_ is currently listed as having a **66 minute runtime**.

‘Doctor Who’ Season 2: “The Reality War” Cast List
--------------------------------------------------

![Image 2: 0hHdj1TV o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/0hHdj1TV_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

The Doctor, portrayed by **Ncuti Gatwa**, leads the charge in this climactic episode. He is joined by his companions: Belinda Chandra, played by **Varada Sethu**, and Ruby Sunday, portrayed by **Millie Gibson**.

Key supporting characters include The Unholy Trinity, comprised of **Mrs. Flood**, whose true identity as the Rani was recently revealed, played by **Anita Dobson**. Joining her side is the recently bi-generated The Rani, played by **Archie Panjabi**, and **[Conrad Clark](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/03/doctor-who-season-2-lucky-day-review/)**, Ruby’s former boyfriend turned antagonist, is portrayed by **Jonah Hauer-King**.

UNIT personnel make significant appearances: The Vlinx, voiced by **Nicholas Briggs**, Kate Lethbridge-Stewart is played by **Jemma Redgrave**, Shirley Bingham by **Ruth Madeley**, and Colonel Christofer Ibrahim by **Alexander Devrient**. Rose Noble returns, played by **Yasmin Finney** and other notable characters include Melanie Bush, portrayed by **Bonnie Langford**, and Susan Triad, played by **Susan Twist**.

![Image 3: wSyFB7Pw o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/wSyFB7Pw_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

![Image 4: 2Hpp3gyO o | Popped](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2Hpp3gyO_o.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

Additional cast members include Poppy, played by **Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps**, who makes her third appearance since first debuting in last season’s opener **_[Space Babies](https://poppednews.com/2024/05/06/doctor-who-season-1-premiere-review/)_**. Ruby’s family members, Carla Sunday and Cherry Sunday, are portrayed by **Michelle Greenidge** and **Angela Wynter**, respectively. **Sam Lawton** and **Nila Aalia** appear elsewhere as Winnie Petheridge and Lakshmi Chandra, respectively.

Where Can I Watch “The Reality War”?
------------------------------------

![Image 5: Varada Sethu, Ncuti Gatwa and Millie Gibson at a table read for 'Doctor Who' Season 2.](https://i0.wp.com/poppednews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Ncuti-Millie-Varada-2-6762aed.jpg?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1)

Credit: BBC Studios

The episode will premiere on **Saturday, May 31st 2025**, during a primetime evening slot of **6:50 pm** on **BBC One**. It will also be available to stream on **BBC iPlayer** at the same time. Unlike earlier episodes this season, **[_“The Reality War”_ will not have an early morning iPlayer release](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/12/doctor-who-season-2-the-reality-war-simultaneous-premiere/)**; instead, it will debut simultaneously with the TV broadcast to ensure a unified viewing experience

For a cinematic experience, over **450 cinemas across the UK and Ireland** will host special screenings of the two-part finale, featuring both _Wish World_ and _The Reality War_, on **May 31**. Tickets can be booked through the official site: [**doctorwhoincinemas.co.uk**](https://www.doctorwhoincinemas.co.uk/).

Outside the UK, _The Reality War_ will be available on **[Disney+](http://disneyplus.com/)** in regions where the service is accessible. The episode will stream simultaneously with the UK broadcast, ensuring fans worldwide can watch together.[](https://cultbox.co.uk/news/episodes-news/doctor-who-finale-will-transmit-simultaneously-worldwide-at-7pm-bt?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

* * *

The first part of the finale, _Wish World_, arrives on **Saturday, May 24,** exclusively on BBC iPlayer from 8am and Disney+ internationally. The concluding episode, _**[The Reality War](https://poppednews.com/2025/05/12/doctor-who-season-2-the-reality-war-simultaneous-premiere/)**_, will premiere with a cinematic flourish on **Saturday, May****31**, debuting simultaneously on BBC One, BBC iPlayer, and in **over 450 cinemas** across the UK and Ireland.

_“The concept of time-travel, paradox and alternate reality has always been mind-blowing and now a mind-blowing novel to live up to it.  Hollywood check this out!”_ — [Bookish Things](http://lesleymc.blogspot.co.uk/2012/03/reality-war-slough-of-despond.html) 5 stars

_“Terse, tense and emotional, the_ _Slough of Despond_ _generates a cool balance between science, history and human relationship.”_ —[The Green Porch](http://davidmarkbrownwrites.com/rrs-roundup-lizard-brains-and-terminal-viscosity/)

In 1992, Radlan Saravanan runs a small business out of a Tudor cottage in the sleepy English village of Elstow. But Radlan was born in 2951, and when he falls in love with a local girl, he has to choose between running from his own people and condemning his lover to die.

He makes _the wrong choice_.

Travelling into the past, falling in love… it turns out that he was _meant_ to do these things. He’s been manipulated all along. But now he’s slipped his handlers, and Time isn’t following the right script any more. Other versions of history vie for dominance, and our human reality is losing.

In 1992, Radlan Saravanan sparked _The Reality War._

[![Image 3](https://timctaylor.files.wordpress.com/2012/01/reality-war2.jpg?w=225&h=300)](http://timctaylor.files.wordpress.com/2012/01/reality-war2.jpg)

_The Reality War_ is a two-novel series loosely inspired by _The Pilgrim’s Progress_, and set in Bedfordshire. It is both an action-adventure series, and a spiritual journey made by two people, mirror images of each other from rival realities.

_The Reality War Book1: The Slough of Despond_ is available now as a Kindle and ePUB eBook, and in paperback.

_The Reality War Book2: The City of Destruction_ is out now for Kindle and ePUB. Paperback edition to follow – expected end of September 2012.

Billie Piper
------------

[![Image 3: RealWorld](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/tardis/images/4/4e/RealWorld.png/revision/latest?cb=20140922173135)](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Tardis:Point_of_view "Tardis:Point of view")

**Billie Paul Piper** (born **Leian Paul Piper**[[1]](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Billie_Piper#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Billie_Piper#cite_note-DWDVDF_126-2) on [22 September](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/22_September_(people) "22 September (people)")[1982](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/1982_(people) "1982 (people)"))[[3]](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Billie_Piper#cite_note-3) is an English actress and singer. She began her career as a [pop](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") singer in her teens, but is now best known for her part as [Rose Tyler](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler"), companion to [the Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), in _[Doctor Who](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_. Following her performance as Rose, she would later return at the end of _[The Reality War](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Reality\_War\_(TV\_story) "The Reality War (TV story)")_ as the "[Sixteenth Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Sixteenth_Doctor "Sixteenth Doctor")".

Pop career
----------

After studying at London-based [Sylvia Young Theatre School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Young_Theatre_School "wikipedia:Sylvia Young Theatre School"), Billie Piper's first break in the entertainment world came as a teenager, when she was selected for a television commercial promoting the pop magazine _[Smash Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash\_Hits "wikipedia:Smash Hits")_. Her role was to run up to the camera, blow a bubble and shout "Pop!" Soon after, she was offered a record deal at the age of fifteen. In 1998 she became the youngest artist ever to debut at number one in the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "wikipedia:UK Singles Chart") with "Because We Want To", released under the single name "Billie". Her follow-up single, "Girlfriend", also debuted at Number One and her first album, _[Honey to the B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey\_to\_the\_B "wikipedia:Honey to the B")_ (released immediately afterwards) debuted at Number 14 in the UK album charts and was certified Platinum for album sales. She released two further singles off the album, "She Wants You" and "Honey to the Bee"; both songs debuted at Number 3.

Piper then took a year to record her second album. She decided to release further records under her full name, Billie Piper. She returned to the Singles Chart in May 2000 with a new, sexier sound. She hit the Number 1 spot with "[Day & Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_%26_Night_(single) "wikipedia:Day & Night (single)")". She waited until the following September to release "[Something Deep Inside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_Deep_Inside "wikipedia:Something Deep Inside")". That reached Number 4 in the UK Singles Chart, but her success wasn't to continue. In October 2000, Piper released her second album, _[Walk of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk\_of\_Life "wikipedia:Walk of Life")_. _Walk of Life_ reached the same chart position as her debut album (#14), but was only certified silver. The song "[Walk of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk_of_Life_(song) "wikipedia:Walk of Life (song)")", the final single off this album, was released in December 2000 and reached Number 25 in the UK Singles Chart due to poor promotion. This proved to be Piper's last musical release, a low-key exit from the world of pop.

In 1999, Piper was nominated for two [Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "wikipedia:Brit Awards") and was named Best Female Star at the _Smash Hits_ Poll Winners' party, although at the latter ceremony she was reduced to tears after being viciously booed by jealous fans of [Ritchie Neville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ritchie_Neville "wikipedia:Ritchie Neville"), member of boyband [5ive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5ive "wikipedia:5ive"), whom she was dating at the time.

Acting career
-------------

In 2003, Piper decided to end her pop career and return to her original ambition, acting. She took acting lessons while living in [Los Angeles](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") and, still a high-profile figure, quickly earned roles in the [BBC](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/BBC "BBC") Television series _[The Canterbury Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Canterbury\_Tales\_(TV\_series) "wikipedia:The Canterbury Tales (TV series)")_ (modern retellings of [Chaucer](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Geoffrey_Chaucer "Geoffrey Chaucer")'s stories) and the one-off drama _[Bella and the Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella\_and\_the\_Boys "wikipedia:Bella and the Boys")_.

Despite the negative reaction usually given to singers who attempt to act, Piper gained very positive reviews for these appearances. Critics seemed to feel that she was a far better actress than a singer.

In 2004, she appeared in the films _[The Calcium Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Calcium\_Kid "wikipedia:The Calcium Kid")_, as the romantic interest of [Orlando Bloom](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Orlando_Bloom "Orlando Bloom")'s character, and _[Things to do Before You're Thirty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Things\_to\_do\_Before\_You%27re\_Thirty "wikipedia:Things to do Before You're Thirty")_. Shortly before starting work on _Doctor Who_ she filmed a starring role in the horror movie _[Spirit Trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit\_Trap "wikipedia:Spirit Trap")_, released in the summer of 2005 to generally poor reviews.

In November 2005, she starred as Hero in a BBC adaptation of _[Much Ado About Nothing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Much\_Ado\_About\_Nothing "wikipedia:Much Ado About Nothing")_, updated in a manner similar to the _Canterbury Tales_ series in which she featured, with Hero a weather presenter in a television station.

After she finished filming for the 2006 season of _Doctor Who_, she began work on _The Ruby in the Smoke_, a BBC adaptation of [Philip Pullman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Pullman "wikipedia:Philip Pullman")'s historical novel. Piper played protagonist [Sally Lockhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sally_Lockhart "wikipedia:Sally Lockhart"), a Victorian orphan. Future [Eleventh Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Eleventh_Doctor "Eleventh Doctor")[Matt Smith](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Smith "Matt Smith") co-starred. The BBC planned to film all four of Pullman's Sally Lockhart novels, presumably with Piper continuing in the role.

### _Doctor Who_

[![Image 4: As Rose Tyler in (2005).](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/tardis/images/e/ef/Rosetyler.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20161114013646)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/tardis/images/e/ef/Rosetyler.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20161114013646)

As Rose Tyler in _[Doctor Who](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_ (2005).

In May 2004, it was announced that Piper was to play [Rose Tyler](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler"), companion to the [Ninth Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Ninth_Doctor "Ninth Doctor") in the revived series of _[Doctor Who](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_, beginning in 2005.

On 25 October 2005, Piper won the Most Popular Actress category at the [National Television Awards](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/National_Television_Awards "National Television Awards") for her work on _Doctor Who_. [BBC News](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/BBC_News "BBC News") named Piper as one of its "Faces of the Year" for 2005, primarily due to her success in _Doctor Who_. At _[The South Bank Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_South\_Bank\_Show "wikipedia:The South Bank Show")_ Awards on 27 January 2006 Piper was awarded _The Times_ Breakthrough Award for her successful transition from singing to acting. In March 2006, the Television and Radio Industries Club named Piper as best new TV talent in their annual Tric awards.

During an October 2006 appearance on _Friday Night with Jonathan Ross_, Piper indicated that she was never a fan of _Doctor Who_ as a child, but her involvement with series had made her enough of a fan that she was now a subscriber to _[Doctor Who Magazine](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doctor\_Who\_Magazine "Doctor Who Magazine")_, which she said she loved. (She proceeded to defend the magazine against jibes made by Ross.) This interview can be heard on the CD release _[Doctor Who at the BBC: The Tenth Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doctor\_Who\_at\_the\_BBC:\_The\_Tenth\_Doctor "Doctor Who at the BBC: The Tenth Doctor")_.

Media rumours that Piper was leaving the show were confirmed when Piper said she'd be leaving at the end of [Series 2](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Series_2_(Doctor_Who) "Series 2 (Doctor Who)") in 2006. However, unknown to the public at large, as Piper later confessed in a 2008 instalment of _[Doctor Who Confidential](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doctor\_Who\_Confidential "Doctor Who Confidential")_, it was already agreed that she would return to the series and she gave misinformation to media about her plans regarding the series.

Piper's last regular appearance on _Doctor Who_ occurred in _[Doomsday](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Doomsday\_(TV\_story) "Doomsday (TV story)")_, which concluded with Rose and the Doctor sharing an emotional farewell as Rose was trapped on a parallel Earth.

### After _Doctor Who_

Following _Doctor Who_, Piper continued to act and was soon cast in the lead role in the sexually explicit drama _Secret Diary of a Call Girl_ which garnered more praise for her acting work. One episode of the series featured an appearance by future [Eleventh Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Eleventh_Doctor "Eleventh Doctor")[Matt Smith](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Matt_Smith "Matt Smith"). The series was a ratings success on both sides of the Atlantic, with its third season broadcast in 2009. Although she was featured in major US media in relation to that series, little reference there has been made to her star-making work on _Doctor Who_.

Despite having moved on to new projects, Piper did not stay away from _Doctor Who_ for long. As noted above, even before her departure in 2006 it had already been arranged for her to return to the series at some point (and there was even a short-lived plan to produce a one-off special featuring her entitled _[Rose Tyler: Earth Defence](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Rose\_Tyler:\_Earth\_Defence "Rose Tyler: Earth Defence")_ which was authorised by the BBC but vetoed by [Russell T Davies](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies")). A short flashback clip of Piper had been included in _[The Runaway Bride](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Runaway\_Bride\_(TV\_story) "The Runaway Bride (TV story)")_, an illustration of her had appeared in _[Human Nature](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Human\_Nature\_(TV\_story) "Human Nature (TV story)")_ and much of the third and fourth series dealt with the Doctor coming to terms with the loss of Rose.

In 2007, rumours began circulating that Piper was to return as Rose in [series 4](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Series_4_(Doctor_Who) "Series 4 (Doctor Who)"), rumours that appeared to be confirmed by paparazzi photographs of her taken on the set of _Doctor Who_. The BBC finally confirmed that Piper would be returning as Rose in the new series and even included her image in the official advance cinema trailer (though her episodes came at the end of the season, they were filmed near the beginning of production). Her first return appearances on _Doctor Who_ were surprise cameos in _[Partners in Crime](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Partners\_in\_Crime\_(TV\_story) "Partners in Crime (TV story)")_, _[The Poison Sky](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Poison\_Sky\_(TV\_story) "The Poison Sky (TV story)")_ and _[Midnight](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Midnight\_(TV\_story) "Midnight (TV story)")_. She returned in earnest for the three-episode finale. Her full-out return in _[Turn Left](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Turn\_Left\_(TV\_story) "Turn Left (TV story)")_ coincided with the American debut of _Secret Diary of a Call Girl_.

Following her appearance in _[Journey's End](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Journey%27s\_End\_(TV\_story) "Journey's End (TV story)")_, Piper again bade farewell to _Doctor Who_ and returned to her work on _Secret Diary of a Call Girl_. However, in 2009, rumours again began circulating of yet another return to the series as [David Tennant](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/David_Tennant "David Tennant") prepared to film his final appearances as the Doctor. Piper made a cameo appearance as a younger version of Rose from before she met the Doctor in _[The End of Time](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_End\_of\_Time\_(TV\_story) "The End of Time (TV story)")_, which first aired on 1 January 2010.

In 2013, Piper played the sentient operating system of [the Moment](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The_Moment "The Moment"), which took on the image of Rose, in the 50th-anniversary episode _[The Day of the Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Day\_of\_the\_Doctor\_(TV\_story) "The Day of the Doctor (TV story)")_. The character was credited as "Rose".

In 2025, Piper made another return to the series when she made a surprise appearance in the [Series 15](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Series_15_(Doctor_Who) "Series 15 (Doctor Who)") finale _[The Reality War](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Reality\_War\_(TV\_story) "The Reality War (TV story)")_ in an undisclosed role. While her appearance at the end of the finale would suggest she was playing the successor to [Ncuti Gatwa](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa")'s [Fifteenth Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor"), the credits for _The Reality War_ only has "And introducing Billie Piper" instead of the usual "And introducing X as the Doctor" for a new actor for the Doctor. The omission of her exact role in the credits, combined with later comments from the BBC and [Russell T Davies](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") regarding her role, has lead to online discussions and debates about the possibility of Piper not actually being the next Doctor after Gatwa's departure.

Personal life
-------------

Piper was born in [Swindon](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Swindon "Swindon"), [Wiltshire](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Wiltshire "Wiltshire"), [England](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/England "England") to Paul and Mandy Piper. Her parents changed her given name from "Leanne" (originally Leiane) three weeks after registering her birth. Billie has one younger brother, Charlie, and two younger sisters, Harley and Ellie.

Piper married [businessman](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Businessman "Businessman"), television presenter, and DJ [Chris Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evans_(presenter) "wikipedia:Chris Evans (presenter)") in May 2001 in [Las Vegas](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). Their marriage attracted much comment due to the sixteen-year age gap between the two. In October 2004, the two began a trial separation. In spring of 2005, it was confirmed that they would be divorcing. The two remained friends and in November 2005 Piper was a guest on the first episode of her ex-husband's show _[OFI Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OFI\_Sunday "wikipedia:OFI Sunday")_.

Piper married actor Laurence Fox, son of [James Fox](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/James_Fox "James Fox"), on 30 December 2007, at St Mary's Church in Easebourne. Her son, Winston James Fox, was born on 21 October 2008.

On 28 October 2011, Piper and her husband announced that she was 15 weeks pregnant with their second child. Piper gave birth to their second son, Eugene Pip Fox, on 5 April 2012.

In 2006, a few months after leaving _Doctor Who_, Piper published an autobiography, _Growing Pains_, in which she discussed her musical career and her time on _Doctor Who_.

Billie Piper shares her birthday, [22 September](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/22_September_(people) "22 September (people)"), with former _Doctor Who_ actor [Frazer Hines](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Frazer_Hines "Frazer Hines"), who played the [Second Doctor](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Second_Doctor "Second Doctor")'s companion [Jamie McCrimmon](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Jamie_McCrimmon "Jamie McCrimmon"). [Billie also exists in the DWU](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/Billie_(The_Gathering) "Billie (The Gathering)"), when her and her birthday were mentioned in the audio story _[The Gathering](https://tardis.fandom.com/wiki/The\_Gathering\_(audio\_story) "The Gathering (audio story)")_.

15.title: Doctor Who: The Reality War cast
15.description: Doctor Who season 15 will come to a dramatic end in The Reality War, an episode full of returning friends & foes. But who stars in it and who do they play?
15.content:
Following the dramatic cliffhanger to Wish World, this week sees the 15th season of [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) come to a close in epic style, with an episode titled The Reality War.

According to the episode's synopsis, it will see battle rage across the skies as the Unholy Trinity unleash their deadly ambition. Meanwhile, the Doctor, Belinda and Ruby have to risk everything in their quest to save one innocent life.

Of course, Ncuti Gatwa, Varada Sethu and Millie Gibson are all back, as are Archie Panjabi, Anita Dobson and Jonah Hauer-King who play the episode's central villains. But who else will we see back for the finale and who do they all play?

Read on for everything you need to know about the cast of Doctor Who season 15 episode 8, The Reality War.

**Who's in the cast of Doctor Who: The Reality War? Full list of characters in season 15 episode 8**
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The main cast for Doctor Who: The Reality War is as follows. Scroll on to find out more about the characters, plus where you may have seen the actors previously.

*   **Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor**
*   **Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra**
*   **Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday**
*   **Archie Panjabi as The Rani**
*   **Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood**
*   **Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark**
*   **Sam Lawton as Winnie Petheridge**
*   **Ruth Madeley as Shirley Bingham**
*   **Michelle Gr****eenidge as Carla Sunday**
*   **Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps as Poppy**
*   **Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge-Stewart**
*   **Susan Twist as Susan Triad**
*   **Alexander Devrient as Colonel Christopher Ibrahim**
*   **Aidan Cook as The Vlinx**
*   **Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble**
*   **Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush**
*   **Angela Wynter as Cherry Sunday**
*   **Nila Aalia as Lakshmi Chandra**

**Ncuti Gatwa plays The Doctor**
--------------------------------

![Image 1: Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who, wearing a blue suit, leaning on a table and looking at the camera](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/517536-b556059.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

**Who is the Doctor?**The Doctor is a time traveller from Gallifrey, and the last of the Time Lords. He travels in space and time in the TARDIS. This version of the character is known as the Fifteenth Doctor, although we know there have been a number of additional incarnations.

**Where have I seen Ncuti Gatwa before?**Beyond his role as the Doctor, Gatwa is best known for his role as Eric Effiong in Sex Education, as well as for starring in [Barbie](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/barbie-review/) and [Masters of the Air](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/masters-of-the-air-release-date/).

**Varada Sethu plays Belinda Chandra**
--------------------------------------

![Image 2: Varada Sethu as her character in Doctor Who, looking concerned under dramatic lighting, wearing a white ribbed top with a collar and subtle jewellery, with blurred studio lights glowing in the background.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521378-c6f8a66.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

**Who is Belinda Chandra?**Belinda is a nurse from London who, in The Robot Revolution, was kidnapped by robots and flown to the stars on their rocket.

At the end of the episode, she told the Doctor to take her home in the TARDIS, but he found himself unable to get back to that particular date, time and location. In The Interstellar Song Contest, they found out this was because the Earth was destroyed on that date. In Wish World, she believed she was married to the Doctor, who was known as John Smith, and that Poppy was their daughter.

**Where have I seen Varada Sethu before?**Sethu is no stranger to Doctor Who, having played Mundy Flynn in last season's episode 3, [Boom](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-varada-sethu-nods-boom-character-exclusive-newsupdate/). She is also known for her roles in series such as [Andor](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/andor-season-3-explained/), Strike Back, Doctor Foster, Hard Sun and [Annika](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/nicola-walker-annika-fourth-wall-comment/), as well as films including Now You See Me 2, [Jurassic World: Dominion](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/scifi/jurassic-world-rebirth-release-date/) and I Came By.

**Millie Gibson plays Ruby Sunday**
-----------------------------------

![Image 3: Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in Doctor Who episode Wish World. She's wearing a red top and denim jacket, with her face lit by the sun, looking into the distance](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520876-0f56101.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Ruby Sunday?**Ruby is the Doctor's former companion, who left the TARDIS to return to her old life after the Doctor helped her find her birth mother. In Wish World, she was seen joining Shirley, Winnie and their team to rebel against Conrad, as she had more access to her old memories than most.

**Where have I seen Millie Gibson before?**Outside of her role in Doctor Who, Gibson is best known for playing Kelly in [Coronation Street](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/coronation-street/), while she has also appeared in Jamie Johnson and Butterfly.

**Archie Panjabi plays The Rani**
---------------------------------

![Image 4: Archie Panjabi as the Rani in Doctor Who. She stands in a rustic wooden cabin, lit by shafts of moody natural light. Wearing a deep red Victorian-style dress under a dark cape, she stares intensely at the camera, flanked by hanging tools and animal pelts.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520878-1550a15.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Archie Panjabi as the Rani in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is the Rani?**In The Interstellar Song Contest, Mrs Flood bi-generated, splitting into two incarnations of the same Time Lady – the second, played by Archie Panjabi, declares herself "The Rani – the definite article".

The Rani is no stranger to long-time Doctor Who fans. A renegade Time Lord and amoral biochemist, she first appeared in the 1980s, portrayed by Kate O'Mara. Known for her ruthless scientific pursuits and disregard for ethical boundaries, The Rani clashed with both the Doctor and the Master in classic stories such as [The Mark of the Rani](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-guide/the-mark-of-the-rani/) and [Time and the Rani](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-guide/time-and-the-rani/). Her last on-screen appearance came in 1993’s charity special Dimensions in Time, but she’s remained a fan favourite, resurfacing in audio dramas and novels, with Siobhan Redmond taking on the role in Big Finish productions.

In Wish World, she was seen using the God of Wishes to create a false reality from the mind of Conrad Clark. Her plan was always to make the Doctor doubt the reality, causing into crumble and open up the Underverse, where she hopes to find Omega.

**Where have I seen Archie Panjabi before?**Panjabi is best known for her Emmy-winning role as Kalinda Sharma in the US TV drama The Good Wife.

Panjabi made early impressions in British films such as East Is East and Bend It Like Beckham, and later gained international recognition for her powerful performances in both television and film. She became the first Asian actor to win a Primetime Emmy Award for acting, earning widespread acclaim for her portrayal of the enigmatic Kalinda.

Beyond The Good Wife, Panjabi has appeared in shows including The Fall, Blindspot, Departure and [Hijack](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/hijack-season-2-apple-tv-release-date/), as well as films like A Mighty Heart.

**Anita Dobson plays Mrs Flood**
--------------------------------

![Image 5: Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who in a black and white outfit](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/523236-cceed68.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Mrs Flood?**As revealed in The Interstellar Song Contest, Mrs Flood is an incarnation of the Doctor’s old nemesis and Time Lady, [the Rani](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-mrs-flood-the-rani-explained/). Ever since The Church on Ruby Road, she has appeared as a mysterious figure, even posing as the next-door neighbour of the Doctor's companions, Ruby Sunday and Belinda Chandra.

She has a habit of speaking directly to the camera and has made many threatening assertions towards the Doctor, although he is yet to become aware of her. In The Interstellar Song Contest, she bi-generated, and is now a subordinate to her next incarnation.

**Where have I seen Anita Dobson before?**Dobson is best known for playing Angie Watts in [EastEnders](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/), while she has also appeared in series including Casualty, [Call the Midwife](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/call-the-midwife-season-15-release-date/), Dodger and [Inside No. 9](https://www.radiotimes.com/going-out/going-out-reviews/inside-no-9-stage-fright-review/), and took part in [Strictly Come Dancing](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/entertainment/strictly-come-dancing-confirms-2025-professionals-newsupdate/) in 2011.

**Jonah Hauer-King plays Conrad Clark**
---------------------------------------

![Image 6: Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark in Doctor Who episode Wish World](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520867-4e355d3.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Jonah Hauer-King as Conrad Clark in Doctor Who episode Wish World.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Conrad Clark?**Conrad is the leader of Think Tank, a group he used to amplify dangerous conspiracy theories about UNIT for financial gain. He previously posed as an alien-obsessed podcaster and struck up a romance with Ruby Sunday to trick her. At the end of Lucky Day, he was freed by Mrs Flood, and is now in league with her and The Rani, creating 'Wish World'.

**Where have I seen Jonah Hauer-King before?**Hauer-King is known for his roles in series including World on Fire, The Flatshare and [The Tattooist of Auschwitz](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/tattooist-of-auschwitz-release-date/), as well as films such as A Dog's Way Home, The Little Mermaid and [William Tell](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/william-tell-review-historical-epic/).

**Sam Lawton plays Winnie Petheridge**
--------------------------------------

![Image 7: Ruth Madeley as Shirley and Sam Lawton as Winnie](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521371-5378229.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ruth Madeley as Shirley and Sam Lawton as Winnie.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Samuel Dore

**Who is Winnie Petheridge?**Winnie is a key member of Shirley's team leading a rebellion against Conrad's rule.

**Where have I seen Sam Lawton before?**Lawton has previously had roles in [Silent Witness](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/silent-witness-season-29-release-date/) and You Don't Know Me.

**Ruth Madeley plays Shirley Anne Bingham**
-------------------------------------------

![Image 8: Ruth Madeley as Shirley in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521370-e4fa772.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ruth Madeley as Shirley in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Samuel Dore

**Who is Shirley Anne Bingham?**Shirley is UNIT's scientific advisor. In Wish World, she was seen leading a rebellion against the tyrannical Conrad.

**Where have I seen Ruth Madeley before?**Madeley has had roles in series including Fresh Meat, [Outnumbered](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/outnumbered-2024-christmas-special-cast/), Cold Feet, Years and Years, The Long Shadow, [Brassic](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/brassic-season-7-sky-release-date/), [Renegade Nell](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/fantasy/renegade-nell-season-2-release/) and [Nightsleeper](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/nightsleeper-season-2-release-date/), as well as films such as [Joy](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/james-norton-big-rt-interview-joy-netflix/) and the TV movie Then Barbara Met Alan.

**Michelle Greenidge plays Carla Sunday**
-----------------------------------------

![Image 9: Michelle Greenidge as Carla Sunday in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2023/12/457020-2d0803c.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Michelle Greenidge as Carla Sunday in Doctor Who.BBC Studios

**Who is Carla Sunday?**Carla is Ruby's adoptive mother.

**Where have I seen Michelle Greenidge before?**Greenidge has previously had roles in series such as It's a Sin, After Life, Mandy, Code 404, The Witchfinder, Alex Rider, Grantchester, Small Axe, [KAOS](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/fantasy/kaos-netflix-season-2-release/) and [Death in Paradise](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/death-in-paradise-season-15-release-date/). She has also had roles in films including Cruella and [Venom: Let There Be Carnage](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/venom-3-release-date-trailer-story/).

**Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps plays Poppy**
-------------------------------------------

![Image 10: Varada Sethu as Belinda and Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps as Poppy in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521373-0b941e4.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda and Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps as Poppy in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Poppy?**Poppy was one of the babies abandoned on Baby Station Beta that the Doctor and Ruby met in Space Babies. At the end of that episode, she and her crew flew to a new planet, but she was recently seen as an apparition, appearing to Belinda in Lagos, Nigeria, in The Story and the Engine. In Conrad’s wish world, Poppy was reimagined as the daughter of Belinda and ‘John Smith’ (aka the Doctor).

**Where have I seen****Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps****before?**Doctor Who is young actor Mavanga-Phipps's only credit thus far.

**Jemma Redgrave plays Kate Lethbridge-Stewart**
------------------------------------------------

![Image 11: Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge Stewart and Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/518799-bd774f9.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge Stewart and Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Kate Lethbridge-Stewart?**Kate is an old friend of the Doctor and the daughter of the Brigadier, who now runs UNIT. In Wish World, Kate was transformed into the leader of the “Unified National Insurance Team”.

**Where have I seen Jemma Redgrave before?**As well as her role in Doctor Who, Redgrave is also known for appearing in series such as Bramwell, Holby City, [Grantchester](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/grantchester-season-10-release-date/) and Silent Witness, as well as films including Howards End, Red, White & Royal Blue and The Beekeeper.

**Susan Twist plays Susan Triad**
---------------------------------

![Image 12: Susan Twist as Susan Triad in Doctor Who, stood at a computer](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521379-1a97496.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Susan Twist as Susan Triad in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Dan Fearon

**Who is Susan Triad?** Susan Triad was previously an angel of death created by Sutekh, who was planted across the universe and timeline wherever the TARDIS landed. One version of her became a tech mogul in 21st century Britain, founding Triad Technology. When Sutekh was defeated, this version of her became a normal human, and was offered a job at UNIT.

**Where have I seen Susan Twist before?** Twist has been seen in Coronation Street and In the Flesh.

**Alexander Devrient plays Colonel Christopher Ibrahim**
--------------------------------------------------------

![Image 13: Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521376-229dc38.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Colonel Christopher Ibrahim?**Colonel Ibrahim is a key soldier at UNIT. Like his comrades, Ibrahim worked at the “Unified National Insurance Team” in Conrad’s wish world.

**Where have I seen Alexander Devrient before?**Devrient has had roles in films such as Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows and The Danish Girl, as well as series including [Emmerdale](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/emmerdale/), [Industry](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/industry-season-4-release-date/), [Motherland](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/amandaland-review/), [Ted Lasso](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/comedy/ted-lasso-season-4-release-date/) and [The Lazarus Project](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/anjli-mohindra-the-lazarus-project-cancellation-gutted-exclusive-newsupdate/).

**Aidan Cook plays The Vlinx**
------------------------------

![Image 14: The Vlinx in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/521377-80a8e12.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

The Vlinx in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is The Vlinx?**The Vlinx a robotic being who works for UNIT, and was first seen in 60th anniversary special The Giggle.

**Where have I seen Aidan Cook before?**As well as playing multiple costumed characters in Doctor Who, Cook has had roles in Fimbles, ZingZillas, Horrid Henry, multiple Star Wars projects and Willow.

**Yasmin Finney****plays****Rose Noble**
----------------------------------------

![Image 15: Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble in Doctor Who's The Legend of Ruby Sunday](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/06/480146-3284954.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble in Doctor Who's The Legend of Ruby Sunday.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Rose Noble?**Rose is the daughter of the Doctor's former companion, Donna Noble. She was last seen working at UNIT in Empire of Death.

**Where have I seen Yasmin Finney before?**As well as her role as Rose in Doctor Who, Finney is best known for playing Elle in Netflix's [Heartstopper](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/heartstopper-season-4-release-date/).

**Bonnie Langford plays Melanie Bush**
--------------------------------------

![Image 16: Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor and Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/05/520875-0d6ab81.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor and Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush in Doctor Who.BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Melanie Bush**? Mel is a companion who first travelled with the Sixth and Seventh Doctors in the classic run of Doctor Who. She returned as a staff member at UNIT in the 60th anniversary specials. In Conrad’s wish world, Melanie was cast as Belinda and John’s neighbour.

**Where have I seen Bonnie Langford before?**Aside from Doctor Who, Langford is known as a theatre icon, and starred as Carmel Kazemi in EastEnders from 2015 to 2018.

**Angela Wynter plays Cherry Sunday**
-------------------------------------

![Image 17: Cherry (Angela Wynter) in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2023/12/457037-b061636.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Cherry (Angela Wynter) in Doctor Who.Lara Cornell/Bad Wolf/BBC Studios 2023

**Who is Cherry Sunday?**Cherry is Carla's mother and therefore Ruby's grandmother.

**Where have I seen Angela Wynter before?**Wynter is best known for playing Yolande in EastEnders, while she has also had roles in series such as Holby City, Cleaning Up, Doctors, Mood, This England, Vampire Academy, [Call the Midwife](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/call-the-midwife-season-15-release-date/), Three Little Birds and Time.

**[Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) continues on Saturday 31st May at 6:50pm on BBC One and BBC iPlayer in the UK. The series is available on Disney+ outside of the UK.**

13.content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This article is about the 2025 series. For the 1977–78 season, see [_Doctor Who_ season 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_season_15 "Doctor Who season 15").

| _Doctor Who_ |
| --- |
| Series 15 |
| [![Image 1: Doctor Who season 2 DVD cover with the Doctor and Yasmin Khan standing on a planet with a backdrop of space and other planets](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/b1/Doctor_Who_Series_15.jpg/250px-Doctor_Who_Series_15.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Doctor_Who_Series_15.jpg) DVD box set cover art |
| Showrunner | [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") |
| Starring | * [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") * [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu") * [Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson") |
| No. of stories | 7 |
| No. of episodes | 8 (+1 special) |
| Release |
| Original network | * [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") * [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") |
| Original release | 12 April– 31 May 2025 |
| Series chronology |
| ←**Previous** [Series 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_14 "Doctor Who series 14") **Next**→ [Series 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_16 "Doctor Who series 16") |
| [List of episodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Doctor_Who_episodes_(2005%E2%80%93present) "List of Doctor Who episodes (2005–present)") |

The fifteenth series of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_television "British television")[science fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_on_television "Science fiction on television") programme _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who "Doctor Who")_ premiered on 12 April 2025. This series is also known as "Season Two" following the production changes and the acquisition of _Doctor Who_'s international broadcasting rights by [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") prior to the previous series. It is the sixth series led by [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") as head writer and executive producer and the second since his return to the show in 2023, having previously worked on it from 2005 to 2010. This series is the fifteenth to air following the programme's revival in 2005, and is the forty-first season overall.

This is the second and final series to star [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") as the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor"), an incarnation of [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), an alien [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord") who travels through time and space in the [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS"), which appears to be a British [police box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_box "Police box") from the outside. [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu") joins the series as new [companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_(Doctor_Who) "Companion (Doctor Who)")[Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra"), with [Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson") also featuring as [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday"), the previous series' companion, for her second and final series in the role. The series was preceded by a [Christmas episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_(Doctor_Who) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)") in December 2024, written by former showrunner and head writer [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat"), where [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") appears as a one-off companion.

The series consists of eight episodes, directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai, [Peter Hoar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hoar "Peter Hoar"), [Amanda Brotchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Brotchie "Amanda Brotchie"), Ben A. Williams, and Makalla McPherson. Alongside Davies, who wrote four episodes and co-wrote a further one, the writers include [Juno Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Dawson "Juno Dawson"), [Inua Ellams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams "Inua Ellams"), [Pete McTighe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_McTighe "Pete McTighe"), and Sharma Angel-Walfall. Filming began in October 2023 and concluded in May 2024.

Notes

1.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_ref-4 "Jump up")**The first seven episodes for the fifteenth series were released simultaneously at 8 a.m. [BST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Summer_Time "British Summer Time") in the United Kingdom on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") (followed by a 7 p.m. BBC One broadcast the same day), and at 12 a.m. [PT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time "Pacific Time") in the United States on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-DWFuton-2) The final episode was released simultaneously at 7 p.m. BST in the United Kingdom on BBC iPlayer and BBC One, and at 11 a.m. PT in the United States on Disney+.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-DWFuton-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-RealityWarReleaseTime-3)
2.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_ref-7 "Jump up")**As seen in "[Midnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_(Doctor_Who) "Midnight (Doctor Who)")" (2008)

[Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") confirmed that he would return for a second series in July 2023.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-8) In November 2023, it was announced that [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") would appear as the companion in the 2024 Christmas special.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-JoytotheWorld-10)[Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson") was revealed to be filming for her second series in November 2023,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Gibson-11) though reports emerged in January 2024 that Gibson would be leaving the show after the fourteenth series, to be replaced by [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-12) However, in April 2024 it was announced that Gibson and Sethu would appear concurrently throughout the series.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-14) Subsequent promotional material foregrounded Gatwa and Sethu as the series' "TARDIS team", highlighting them as the first to consist solely of people of colour, with Gibson described as an "outgoing series regular".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-15) Gibson appeared in the fourth episode, "[Lucky Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Day_(Doctor_Who) "Lucky Day (Doctor Who)")", and appears in the seventh and eighth episodes, "[Wish World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_World "Wish World")" / "[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-16) Sethu made a surprise appearance in the series prior in "[Boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_(Doctor_Who) "Boom (Doctor Who)")" (2024) as Mundy Flynn before her debut as the new companion. On 27 July, it was announced at [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con") that Sethu's character would be called Belinda Chandra.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-17) It is later revealed in "[The Robot Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Robot_Revolution "The Robot Revolution")" that Mundy is a descendant of Belinda.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-18)

[Alan Cumming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Cumming "Alan Cumming") guest starred in "[Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_(Doctor_Who) "Lux (Doctor Who)")" as a cartoon character named "Mr Ring-a-Ding"; he had previously appeared in the show as King [James VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_VI "James VI") in "[The Witchfinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witchfinders "The Witchfinders")" (2018). Davies stated that only Cumming could give the character "so much wit, malice, danger and fun".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1)[Rose Ayling-Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Ayling-Ellis "Rose Ayling-Ellis")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-19) and [Christopher Chung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Chung_(actor) "Christopher Chung (actor)") appears in "[The Well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Well_(Doctor_Who) "The Well (Doctor Who)")" as [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper") also returned to _Doctor Who_ after previously portraying the Doctor's companion [Rose Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler") last appearing in the 2013 fiftieth anniversary special, "[The Day of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Day_of_the_Doctor "The Day of the Doctor")",[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-36) when the Fifteenth Doctor regenerates into a character portrayed by her at the end of the episode.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-37) While Piper's official role remains undisclosed, with the closing credits merely reading "Introducing Billie Piper",[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-38) some sources assumed her to be taking on the Doctor's sixteenth incarnation.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-finalncuti-41)

Similar to the [fourteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_(series_14) "Doctor Who (series 14)"), the fifteenth series consists of a Christmas special followed by eight regular episodes, consisting of six standalone episodes and a two-part finale.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024c6-42) The synopsis of the series was officially stated to be about an "epic quest" getting Belinda back to Earth, as the TARDIS team face "wider terrors than ever before".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1)

Davies was writing the 2024 Christmas special by December 2022,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies20227-43) and the fifteenth series by June 2023.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-44) By 18 September 2023, five of the nine scripts had been completed according to Davies's column in _[Doctor Who Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who\_Magazine "Doctor Who Magazine")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies202311-45) By 2 January 2024, Davies's column stated that the fifth episode was now on Draft 5, while Episode 6 was about to enter Draft 9, "getting this script ready has been epic...but all worth it, what a story!"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024b8-46)

In May 2024, former showrunner and head writer [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat") confirmed that he had written the 2024 Christmas special, and that it was entitled "[Joy to the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_(Doctor_Who) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)")".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-JoytotheWorld-10) The episodes of the series itself were written by Davies and four other writers,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024a10-47) revealed on 27 January 2025 to be [Juno Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Dawson "Juno Dawson"), [Inua Ellams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams "Inua Ellams"), [Pete McTighe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_McTighe "Pete McTighe"), and Sharma Angel-Walfall.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-48)

With filming for the [previous series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_14 "Doctor Who series 14") concluding in July 2023, crew were given a four-week turnaround before [pre-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-production "Pre-production") started for the next series, on 14 August.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock202312-49) Each production block was given ten weeks of preparation.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024b10-50) The first [readthrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read-through "Read-through") was held on 17 October 2023.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024a12-51)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on 23 October 2023 at Bad Wolf Studios, with the 2024 Christmas special "Joy to the World" assigned to the first block, directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn20234-52)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024a12-51)

The second block – containing the [first](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Robot_Revolution "The Robot Revolution") and [fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Day_(Doctor_Who) "Lucky Day (Doctor Who)") episodes – had its first readthrough on 7 November 2023,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Episode_BTS-53)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024b10-50) and began filming on 14 November 2023, directed by [Peter Hoar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hoar "Peter Hoar").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024b10-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn20234-52) Hoar had previously directed the [sixth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_6 "Doctor Who series 6") episode "[A Good Man Goes to War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Man_Goes_to_War "A Good Man Goes to War")" (2011), and had worked with Davies on _[It's a Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s\_A\_Sin\_(TV\_series) "It's A Sin (TV series)")_ and _[Nolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nolly\_(TV\_series) "Nolly (TV series)")_.

Filming for the third block – containing the [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_(Doctor_Who) "Lux (Doctor Who)") and [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Well_(Doctor_Who) "The Well (Doctor Who)") episodes – began on Monday 8 January 2024 after the Christmas break,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024a6-54) directed by [Amanda Brotchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Brotchie "Amanda Brotchie").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024b8-46)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024b4-55) Location filming at [Penarth Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penarth_Pier "Penarth Pier") marked the first time that Sethu was photographed on-set as the new companion.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-56)

Makalla McPherson and Ben A. Williams directed further blocks, with McPherson directing the [fifth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine") episode, where she described she had "created a unique crane shot as the Doctor runs through a maze as they escape their captors" [[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024b4-55) and Williams directing the sixth episode, which he described as a "very big episode", and Davies described as "epic".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Williams-57)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024b8-46)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024c6-58)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024c6-42) The episode from Williams is themed after the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest "Eurovision Song Contest").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-insta-59)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-60) Production for the series wrapped on 24 May 2024.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-61)

On 21 February 2025, a trailer stating that the series would launch on 12 April was shown during the BBC's coverage of a [Six Nations Under 20s Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Six_Nations_Under_20s_Championship "2025 Six Nations Under 20s Championship") rugby match between England and Scotland.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-12April-67) The series is released in the [UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK "UK") on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") and internationally on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies202311-45)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Disney-68)

The episodes are released weekly on Saturdays at 8 a.m. [BST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Summer_Time "British Summer Time").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1) Episodes also air on the evening of their release on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-69) The sixth episode of the series, "[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Interstellar_Song_Contest "The Interstellar Song Contest")", was scheduled to be broadcast on BBC One on 17 May, ahead of the final of the [Eurovision Song Contest 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2025 "Eurovision Song Contest 2025"). However, if the [FA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FA_Cup_final "2025 FA Cup final"), which was also scheduled to be played that afternoon, went to [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time"), the episode would not be shown on BBC One.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-70) The two-part finale, "Wish World" / "The Reality War", were screened together in UK cinemas on 31 May. Release of "The Reality War" across streaming and cinemas and internationally aligned with its simultaneous evening BBC One broadcast. The episode was released at 6:50 p.m. BST in the United Kingdom, and at 11 a.m. PT in the United States.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-71)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-RealityWarReleaseTime-3)

Due to the terms of a deal between [BBC Worldwide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Worldwide "BBC Worldwide") and [SMG Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Media_Group "Shanghai Media Group") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in May 2017, the company has first [right of refusal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_of_first_refusal "Right of first refusal") on the purchase for the Chinese market of future series of the programme until and including series 15.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-72)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-73)

The series is accompanied by _[Doctor Who: Unleashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who:\_Unleashed "Doctor Who: Unleashed")_, a behind-the-scenes companion show. Adopting a similar format to the former behind-the-scenes programme _[Doctor Who Confidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Who\_Confidential "Doctor Who Confidential")_, _Unleashed_ follows every new episode of _Doctor Who_ with a 30-minute instalment on [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three"), hosted by [Steffan Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steffan_Powell "Steffan Powell").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-75)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-UnleashedS2-76)
